title: 弘治二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣東鄉試錄序
聖天子紹統之初聿新萬化以風
四海而尤銳意於求賢廣東
雖南極海陬然風聲所至不
數月而浹又明年是為弘治
二年大比之年也是舉也在
祖宗列聖為屢舉在
===
皇上則首舉且所注意者維時今
都察院右都御史屠滽總督
其地祗若
休命為一方先比試之前四月
適有
召命而右都御史秦紘寔代之
下車之初謂
punctuated:
廣東鄉試錄序

聖天子紹統之初，聿新萬化，以風四海，而尤銳意於求賢。廣東雖南極海陬，然風聲所至，不數月而浹。又明年，是為弘治二年，大比之年也。是舉也，在祖宗列聖為屢舉，在皇上則首舉，且所注意者。維時，今都察院右都御史屠滽總督其地，祗若休命，為一方先。比試之前四月，適有召命，而右都御史秦紘寔代之。下車之初，謂
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination

At the beginning of his succession to the imperial line, the sage Son of Heaven renewed all aspects of governance to influence all within the Four Seas, and devoted himself especially to seeking worthy men. Although Guangdong lies at the southern extremity, in a remote corner by the sea, the influence of his example spread throughout it within a few months. The following year was the second year of Hongzhi [1489], a year of the triennial examination. Under the successive sage emperors, his ancestors, this examination had been held many times; for His Majesty, it was the first, and a matter of particular concern.

At that time, Tu Yong 屠滽, now Right Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate, was serving as Supreme Commander over the region. Reverently complying with the gracious imperial command, he set an example for the whole region. title: 弘治二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
維新之政惟是為重尤加意焉
一時如太監韋眷總鎮於茲
罔不協力太監王宣安遠侯
柳景亦以有事茲土賛襄不
後然始終其事矢殫心力者
監察御史周南也于時實監
臨焉若提調則左參政蔣雲漢
===
左參議姜英監試則副使李
士實僉事戴中考試則教諭吳
清周服同考試則學正章晟
教諭柯德賛朱麒訓導章英劉
禮而左布政使熊懷右布政
使謝瑀按察使李瑢陶魯右
參政張玘副使翁晏陳英右

title: 弘治二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
叅議周宏僉事周啓李元鎮陸
遠董榮韋斌王經又先已各
極鼓鑄相成之道於他日考
試者以禮聘至其餘百執事
以材選待試之士幾千人七
日而三試之拔其尤者七十
有五人錄三塲文字二十篇
===
合所與共事於兹者得四十
有一人自始事至終事二十
有二日胥惕惕焉毋敢分晝
夜視爲易事有遺力焉凡以
求當
上心而已蓋
祖宗憲典在天下有不待申飭而

title: 弘治二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
克嵗謹一嵗以不失其初意
如當日者莫科舉若而天下
又畧相同又况為
聖意所嚮敢少忽哉若我
國家之所以為教則又盡黜百
家而一以聖賢之道教成則
舉而用之欲其以是行也是
===
道也人之所自有非自外至
取之於己約以亷極之於天
下大無不該而小不遺焉故
以之事親則為孝子以之事
君則為忠臣以之治國平天
下則國治而天下平無所往
而不可亦無往而可離也三
punctuated: 克嵗謹一嵗，以不失其初意如當日者，莫科舉若，而天下又畧相同。又况為聖意所嚮，敢少忽哉？若我國家之所以為教，則又盡黜百家，而一以聖賢之道。教成則舉而用之，欲其以是行也。是道也，人之所自有，非自外至。取之於己，約以亷；極之於天下，大無不該，而小不遺焉。故以之事親則為孝子，以之事君則為忠臣，以之治國平天下則國治而天下平。無所往而不可，亦無往而可離也。三
translation_en: …can be observed more scrupulously with each passing year, preserving their original intent as on the day they were established: in this respect, nothing equals the civil-service examinations, and practice is broadly similar throughout the realm. Moreover, since they are the object of the imperial will, dare we neglect them even slightly? As for the instruction provided by our dynasty, it excludes all the Hundred Schools and relies exclusively upon the Way of the sages and worthies. Once men have completed their education, they are selected and employed, with the intention that they put this Way into practice. This Way is something people inherently possess; it does not come from outside. Sought within oneself, it is simple and restrained [?]; extended throughout the realm, it encompasses everything great and omits nothing small. Thus, by serving one's parents through it, one becomes a filial son; by serving one's ruler through it, one becomes a loyal minister; and by governing the state and bringing peace to all under Heaven through it, the state becomes well governed and all under Heaven becomes peaceful. Wherever one goes, it is applicable; nowhere can one depart from it. The Three…

title: 弘治二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
代以前固嘗以是為教士亦
以是用其後夷霸雜而華實
偏得失相半不敢復議於斯
起而更張之不能不有待於
我
朝况又重之以求賢汲汲如
今日哉士生其間亦何幸歟而
===
其所以為用必竭其所得以
自効毋留藏焉庶於
朝家教而用之之意為得而亦
可少仗是以報
上若或以為魚兎之筌蹄而棄之
而自壞焉則將有議其後者
矣豈所望哉
punctuated: 代以前，固嘗以是為教，士亦以是用。其後夷霸雜而華實偏，得失相半，不敢復議於斯。起而更張之，不能不有待於我朝。况又重之以求賢汲汲如今日哉！士生其間，亦何幸歟！而其所以為用，必竭其所得以自効，毋留藏焉。庶於朝家教而用之之意為得，而亦可少仗是以報上。若或以為魚兎之筌蹄而棄之，而自壞焉，則將有議其後者矣，豈所望哉？
translation_en:
…before the Three Dynasties, this indeed served as the basis of instruction, and scholars were likewise employed on this basis. Thereafter, barbarian ways and hegemonic practices became intermingled, outward refinement and substance fell out of balance, and gains and losses were equally divided. I dare not discuss this further here. For someone to arise and reform these practices, it was necessary to await our dynasty. How much more fortunate it is that this has been reinforced by so eager a search for worthy men as we see today! How fortunate, indeed, are scholars born in such a time!

When they enter service, they must devote all they have acquired to fulfilling their duties, holding nothing back. Only then may they fulfill the court’s intention in educating and employing them, and thereby repay, in some small measure, His Majesty. Should any regard this learning as a fish trap or rabbit snare, to be discarded once its purpose has been served, and thus bring about their own ruin, there will surely be those who criticize them afterward. How could this be what we hope for?

問：自古帝王之一天下，必有非常之德而成非常之功。三代以前，迹皆經見；自是以後，姑未暇言。仰惟我太祖高皇帝，援四海於胡塵，成一代之帝業，德冠百王，功蓋萬世。逮我憲宗純皇帝，思求至治，惟率舊章，爰輯簡編，續為綱目。宋元之事蹟不遺，而皇明之謨烈益著。天下臣民，家傳人誦。請以我烈祖之神功聖德言之。夫首帝堯之德，於以見大哉
translation_en:
Five legal judgments
1. Failing to report a matter that ought to be reported to the throne.
2. The market office’s assessment of commodity prices.
3. Buddhist monks and Daoist priests bowing to their parents.
4. Failing to drill soldiers.
5. Refusing to accept a complaint for adjudication.

Third Session
Five policy questions
Question: From antiquity, emperors and kings who unified All Under Heaven invariably possessed extraordinary virtue and accomplished extraordinary deeds. The deeds of the Three Dynasties and earlier times are all recorded in the classics; for the moment, there is no leisure to discuss those of subsequent times. Reverently we consider how our Emperor Taizu Gao rescued all within the Four Seas from the dust of Hu domination and established the imperial enterprise of a dynasty. His virtue surpassed that of a hundred kings, and his achievements overshadowed those of all ages. Then our Emperor Xianzong Chun, seeking perfect government and following the established precedents, compiled historical writings to continue the Outline and Details (Gangmu). No deeds of the Song and Yuan were omitted, while the plans and glorious achievements of our august Ming became still more manifest. Throughout the realm, officials and commoners transmit it in every household and recite it individually. Please discuss the wondrous achievements and sagely virtue of our illustrious progenitor. By giving first place to Emperor Yao’s virtue, it thereby reveals how great …

title: 弘治二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
帝王之道師孔子之言於以見大哉
帝王之學安民以仁一如天之仁也推誠相與
一動物之誠也討溫台而戒毋縱殺
取文石而慮爲厲民其與湯之寛文
之仁世異而心同虜前元宗属而還
之釋前元皇孫而侯之其與釋箕子
封微子迹殊而心一書古人行事於
殿壁書大學衍義於兩廡其亦學于
古訓歟毀陳友諒之鏤金床却方國
===
珍之寶鞍轡其亦不貴異物歟是
聖德寔冠百王而無前也在太平而稱爲神武
不殺者何所指議江州而稱爲師直
爲壯者何所見鄱陽旣捷直趨武昌
僞漢可蕩平矣何以復待他日之諭
降三郡來歸遣還質子國珍已降附
矣何以復勞他日之致討
王師始於何地伊誰以千艘來歸
帝業成於何年伊誰以半夜北遁禮樂興材能
punctuated:
帝王之道；師孔子之言，於以見大哉帝王之學。安民以仁，一如天之仁也；推誠相與，一動物之誠也。討溫台而戒毋縱殺，取文石而慮爲厲民，其與湯之寛、文之仁，世異而心同。虜前元宗属而還之，釋前元皇孫而侯之，其與釋箕子、封微子，迹殊而心一。書古人行事於殿壁，書大學衍義於兩廡，其亦學于古訓歟？毀陳友諒之鏤金床，却方國珍之寶鞍轡，其亦不貴異物歟？是聖德寔冠百王而無前也。
在太平而稱爲神武不殺者，何所指？議江州而稱爲師直爲壯者，何所見？鄱陽旣捷，直趨武昌，僞漢可蕩平矣，何以復待他日之諭降？三郡來歸，遣還質子，國珍已降附矣，何以復勞他日之致討？王師始於何地？伊誰以千艘來歸？帝業成於何年？伊誰以半夜北遁？禮樂興，材能
translation_en:
…the Way of emperors and kings; taking Confucius’s words as his guide reveals how great is the learning of emperors and kings. He brought peace to the people through benevolence, just like Heaven’s benevolence; he dealt with others in utter sincerity—a sincerity that moved all beings [?]. When campaigning against Wen and Tai, he forbade indiscriminate killing; when acquiring patterned stone, he worried that it would burden the people. Compared with Tang’s magnanimity and King Wen’s benevolence, the ages differed, but the heart was the same. He captured members of the former Yuan ruling house and sent them back; he released a grandson of the former Yuan emperor and made him a marquis. Compared with releasing Jizi and enfeoffing Weizi, the deeds differed, but the heart was one. He had the deeds of the ancients inscribed on the palace walls and the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning inscribed in the two side galleries. Was this not also learning from ancient teachings? He destroyed Chen Youliang’s gold-ornamented bed and rejected Fang Guozhen’s precious saddle and bridle. Was this not also refusing to prize exotic objects? His sagely virtue indeed surpassed that of all former kings and was without precedent.
When, at Taiping, he was praised for divine martial prowess without killing, what did this refer to? When discussing Jiangzhou [?], what was perceived that prompted the saying, “An army whose cause is just is strong”? After victory at Poyang, he advanced straight toward Wuchang, and the illegitimate Han regime could have been swept away. Why, then, did he await a later occasion to issue an edict calling for its surrender? The three prefectures submitted, and he sent back the sons held as hostages. Guozhen had already surrendered and pledged allegiance; why, then, was another punitive expedition later required? Where did the imperial army first arise? Who came over to him with a thousand vessels? In what year was the imperial enterprise accomplished? Who fled north at midnight? Rites and music flourished, and men of talent…

title: 弘治二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
舉則有廟社樂舞之制文武取士之
科文儒崇絃誦作則有禮賢館之重
五經師之尊是
神功寔盖萬世而莫並也竊以謂
聖子神孫思欲光乎前而裕乎後不過脩其德
而纘其功
純皇纂述之意其在兹哉不識此語誠然乎戎
稽於簡冊踈其事槩亦可以見諸生
之服膺
===
明訓也
問為治莫要於敬大臣尤莫要於納諫諍
夫廉遠堂高投鼠忌器體貌大臣國
家常典彼相國尊官也而猶不免械
繫之辱抑劔履上殿者非出於誠心
乎太尉重任也而猶竟有詔獄之下
抑朝禮益莊者果徒事虚文乎不免
長沙之謫又何益於前席之召問終
有赤族之加又何必於麟閣之不名
punctuated:
舉，則有廟社樂舞之制、文武取士之科；文儒崇，絃誦作，則有禮賢館之重、五經師之尊。是神功寔盖萬世而莫並也。竊以謂，聖子神孫思欲光乎前而裕乎後，不過脩其德而纘其功。純皇纂述之意，其在兹哉！不識此語誠然乎？戎稽於簡冊，踈其事槩，亦可以見諸生之服膺明訓也。

問：為治莫要於敬大臣，尤莫要於納諫諍。夫廉遠堂高，投鼠忌器，體貌大臣，國家常典。彼相國，尊官也，而猶不免械繫之辱，抑劔履上殿者非出於誠心乎？太尉，重任也，而猶竟有詔獄之下，抑朝禮益莊者果徒事虚文乎？不免長沙之謫，又何益於前席之召問？終有赤族之加，又何必於麟閣之不名？
translation_en:
…were promoted: there were regulations for music and dance at the ancestral temple and the altars of soil and grain, and examination categories for selecting civil and military men. Learned scholars were honored, and the sounds of stringed instruments and recitation arose: there was the esteem accorded to the Hall for Honoring Worthies and the reverence shown to teachers of the Five Classics. These divine achievements truly surpass those of all ages and have no equal. I venture to say that, when sagely sons and divine grandsons wish to bring glory to their predecessors and provide abundantly for their successors, they need only cultivate their virtue and carry on their achievements. Surely herein lay Emperor Chun’s intention in continuing and transmitting his predecessor’s work! I wonder whether this statement is indeed correct. Consult the written records [?] and set out the broad outlines of these events; this will also reveal how you students have taken the illustrious instructions to heart.

Question: In governing, nothing is more essential than respecting the great ministers, and still more essential is accepting remonstrance. A lofty hall has a long flight of steps; one hesitates to throw something at a rat for fear of damaging the vessel beside it. Treating great ministers with dignity and courtesy is an established rule of the state. The Chancellor of State held an honored office, yet even he could not escape the humiliation of being put in fetters. Could it be that permission to ascend the hall wearing his sword and shoes was not granted sincerely? The Defender-in-Chief bore weighty responsibilities, yet he too was ultimately committed to prison by imperial command. Could it be that the increasingly solemn courtesies at court were indeed merely empty formalities? If banishment to Changsha could not be avoided, what benefit was there in summoning him for questioning and moving forward on the mat toward him? If extermination of his clan was ultimately imposed, why bother omitting his personal name in the Qilin Pavilion? …

title: 弘治二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
山南夜召喜見顏色胡卒莫去其追
仇盡言之恨曲江召宴愛形詩章然
終莫救其信讒投閑之譴親幸其第
問以後事其與盟血未乾兎死狗烹
者何矛盾歟定策兩朝畧無疑隙其
與驂乗致疑心不自安者何枘鑿歟
君之視臣如手足則臣視君如腹心
君臣一體心貌相符何道而致是歟
誹木諫鼓明目達聰詢及芻蕘國家
===
美政彼內多慾而外施仁義諫直也
何以竟綰淮南之綬憂其末而忘其
本言忠也胡為僅改平原之任外戚
竊柄人所難言而戒之者誰歟佞臣
誤國人誰敢議而劾之者誰歟斬錯
之爭聞者毛竦或疑其為復讐之舉
子虛之作見者心醉何又啓其神仙
之想叩頭流血心本狥國而世何以
賣直加之叩鐶大呼心本忘家而人
punctuated: 山南夜召，喜見顏色，胡卒莫去其追仇盡言之恨？曲江召宴，愛形詩章，然終莫救其信讒投閑之譴。親幸其第，問以後事，其與盟血未乾、兎死狗烹者，何矛盾歟？定策兩朝，畧無疑隙，其與驂乗致疑、心不自安者，何枘鑿歟？君之視臣如手足，則臣視君如腹心。君臣一體，心貌相符，何道而致是歟？誹木諫鼓，明目達聰，詢及芻蕘，國家美政。彼內多慾而外施仁義，諫直也，何以竟綰淮南之綬？憂其末而忘其本，言忠也，胡為僅改平原之任？外戚竊柄，人所難言，而戒之者誰歟？佞臣誤國，人誰敢議，而劾之者誰歟？斬錯之爭，聞者毛竦，或疑其為復讐之舉。子虛之作，見者心醉，何又啓其神仙之想？叩頭流血，心本狥國，而世何以賣直加之？叩鐶大呼，心本忘家，而人
translation_en:
At the nighttime summons in Shannan, delight showed on the ruler’s face. Why, in the end, could he not relinquish his resentment and his wish to take revenge for utterly frank speech? When Qujiang was summoned to a banquet, affection found expression in verse; yet this ultimately could not save him from the punishment of being relegated to inactivity when the ruler believed slander. A ruler personally visited his minister’s residence and consulted him about affairs after his own death: how contradictory was this to killing the hound once the hare was dead, before the blood of their covenant had even dried! A minister helped settle the succession in two reigns without the slightest suspicion or estrangement: how incompatible was this with suspicion arising over a companion in the imperial carriage, leaving the minister uneasy at heart! When a ruler regards his ministers as his hands and feet, they regard him as their belly and heart. By what way can ruler and ministers become one body, with inward feelings and outward conduct in accord?

Posts for criticism and drums for remonstrance, opening the ruler’s eyes and ears, and consulting even grass-cutters and wood-gatherers: these are admirable practices of government. To say that a ruler harbored many desires within while outwardly practicing benevolence and righteousness was forthright remonstrance. Why, then, did its author end up wearing the seal-cord of an appointment in Huainan? To say that a ruler worried about the branches while forgetting the root was loyal speech. Why did it result merely in a transfer to a post in Pingyuan? When imperial relatives usurped authority, something people found difficult to speak about, who warned against it? When flattering ministers brought the state to ruin, something no one dared criticize, who impeached them? The protest over the execution of Chao Cuo made listeners’ hair stand on end, yet some suspected it was an act of vengeance. The composition “Master Zixu” entranced its readers; why did it also awaken the ruler’s longing for divine immortals? He knocked his head against the ground until it bled, intending at heart to sacrifice himself for the state: why did the world accuse him of parading his rectitude? He struck the gate-ring and cried aloud, his heart heedless of his own family; yet people …

title: 弘治二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
胡以過激譏之納約自牖周易之云
忠臣良臣唐賢所別耳目聰明流通
弗滯何脩而得此歟願酌其中行將
獻之
上
問闢異端所以崇正道也異端之害而佛
氏為尤甚諸儒闢之而胡氏為獨詳
觀於崇正辯可見已且人道莫大於
三綱而佛氏則淪之人情不外乎四
===
端而佛氏則絕之論治人治國之要
而妄以為堯舜之風立歸空入善之
說而妄以詆周孔之道內乖天屬而
謂不違其孝外缺奉主而謂不失其
敬果何說歟與上人言而謂依於仁
與下人言而謂依於禮又何說歟生
之後死之前人所當盡心者何以專
為前生後生之說天之下地之上人
所共屬目者何以別立天上地下之
punctuated:
胡以過激譏之？納約自牖，《周易》之云；忠臣、良臣，唐賢所別。耳目聰明，流通弗滯，何脩而得此歟？願酌其中，行將獻之上。

問：闢異端所以崇正道也。異端之害，而佛氏為尤甚；諸儒闢之，而胡氏為獨詳。觀於《崇正辯》，可見已。且人道莫大於三綱，而佛氏則淪之；人情不外乎四端，而佛氏則絕之。論治人治國之要，而妄以為堯舜之風；立歸空入善之說，而妄以詆周孔之道。內乖天屬，而謂不違其孝；外缺奉主，而謂不失其敬，果何說歟？與上人言，而謂依於仁；與下人言，而謂依於禮，又何說歟？生之後，死之前，人所當盡心者，何以專為前生後生之說？天之下，地之上，人所共屬目者，何以別立天上地下之
translation_en:
…why did people criticize him for being excessively vehement? “Present restrained counsel through the window” is a saying of the Book of Changes; “loyal ministers” and “good ministers” were distinguished by a worthy of the Tang. Through what cultivation can one attain keen hearing and clear sight, with communication flowing freely and without obstruction? Please weigh the proper balance in these matters; your response will presently be submitted to His Majesty.

Question: Refuting heterodox teachings serves to exalt the correct Way. Among the harms caused by heterodox teachings, those of Buddhism are especially grave; among the Confucian scholars who have refuted it, Master Hu has been uniquely thorough. This can be seen in his Defense of Orthodoxy (Chongzheng bian). Nothing in the human Way is greater than the Three Bonds, yet Buddhism subverts them; human moral feelings are encompassed by the Four Beginnings, yet Buddhism cuts them off. It discusses the essentials of governing people and the state, falsely claiming to embody the spirit of Yao and Shun; it establishes doctrines of returning to emptiness and entering goodness, presumptuously using them to disparage the Way of the Duke of Zhou and Confucius. Within the family, it violates natural kinship ties, yet claims not to contravene filial piety; outside the family, it neglects service to the ruler, yet claims not to fail in reverence. What justification can there actually be for this? When speaking with those above, its adherents claim to rely on benevolence; when speaking with those below, they claim to rely on ritual propriety. What justification is there for this, either? What people ought to devote their minds to lies after birth and before death: why, then, concentrate exclusively on doctrines of previous and future lives? What all people see lies beneath heaven and above earth: why, then, separately establish designations for what is above heaven and below earth…

title: 弘治二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
名等慈悲也不及其父母妻子而及
虎狼蛇虺可乎等棄舍也獨使人棄
財舍僧不使僧棄財與人得乎河山
大地必欲空之而卒不可空兵刑災
禍必欲度之而卒不獲度以上而崇
其敎者何人而欲毁之者又何人以
下而泥其法者何人而力詆之者又
何人曰惑曰懼曰貪今世之蔽何所
歸曰立德曰立功曰立言吾人之志
===
其何嚮是皆吾儒所當講不可一日
廢也亦不得已而有言也幸盡言之
以觀所學
問國之治忽係君子小人之進退君人者
不可以不知也是故牛口之下賤矣
曾以之而成霸圖草廬之中微矣曾
以之而成王業回紇之羅拜以何人
為重輕淮蔡之蕩平係何人之用捨
稱為得人耶律之語將安歸戒毋生
punctuated:
名？等慈悲也，不及其父母妻子而及虎狼蛇虺，可乎？等棄舍也，獨使人棄財舍僧，不使僧棄財與人，得乎？河山大地，必欲空之，而卒不可空；兵刑災禍，必欲度之，而卒不獲度。以上而崇其敎者何人，而欲毁之者又何人？以下而泥其法者何人，而力詆之者又何人？曰惑、曰懼、曰貪，今世之蔽何所歸？曰立德、曰立功、曰立言，吾人之志其何嚮？是皆吾儒所當講，不可一日廢也，亦不得已而有言也。幸盡言之，以觀所學。
問：國之治忽，係君子小人之進退，君人者不可以不知也。是故牛口之下，賤矣，曾以之而成霸圖；草廬之中，微矣，曾以之而成王業。回紇之羅拜，以何人為重輕？淮蔡之蕩平，係何人之用捨？稱為得人，耶律之語將安歸？戒毋生
translation_en:
…such designations? If compassion is to be the same for all, is it acceptable to extend it to tigers, wolves, snakes, and vipers, but not to one's parents, wife, and children? If renunciation and giving are to be the same for all, is it right to make people relinquish their wealth and give it to monks, without making monks relinquish their wealth and give it to others? They insist on rendering rivers, mountains, and the great earth empty, yet ultimately cannot empty them; they insist on deliverance from warfare, punishments, calamities, and misfortunes, yet ultimately cannot attain that deliverance. Among those above, who revered this teaching, and who wished to destroy it? Among those below, who clung to its doctrines, and who vigorously denounced them? Delusion, fear, and greed: to which should the blindness of the present age be attributed? Establishing virtue, establishing achievements, and establishing enduring words: toward which should our aspirations turn? These are all matters that we Confucian scholars ought to examine, and we must not neglect them for a single day. They are also matters on which we cannot but speak. Please discuss them fully, so that we may see what you have learned.
Question: Whether a state is well governed or neglected depends on the advancement or dismissal of gentlemen and petty men. A ruler of men must understand this. Thus, tending cattle was a lowly occupation, yet someone in that station enabled the realization of a hegemon's ambitions; dwelling in a thatched cottage was an obscure existence, yet someone in that position enabled the founding of a kingly enterprise. On whose presence or absence did the Huihe's bowing in ranks depend? On whose employment or dismissal did the pacification of Huai and Cai depend? In praising the choice of a worthy man, to whom did Yelü's words refer? In the admonition, “Do not stir up…”

title: 弘治二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
事遼人之望將奚属三苗之竄何遽
形於攝位之際兩觀之誅何遽見於
攝相之初國賊之刑一正而眠者始
帖席矣司戶之貶一行而市井皆相
賀焉脫距之詩作而庶民歌於道拔
釘之謡徵而士論快於朝吾今召君
似知其賢天下必肥似知其忠能用
之乎譽樹不已知其佞矣忌賢無比
知其奸矣能去之乎夫既往之迹固
===
歷歷可指而
維新之政則蕩蕩難名取於眾善之中以匡
一代之治亦可以見諸生致用之學
問廣東為地北距五嶺以達京國南負重
溟以受島夷亦南陬一大都會也自
入我
朝百二十年仁漸義摩遭逢
列聖化行俗美無間十州然覆盆之地日月或
遺其明而吹律之谷陽春尚有所待
punctuated:
事，遼人之望將奚属？三苗之竄，何遽形於攝位之際？兩觀之誅，何遽見於攝相之初？國賊之刑一正，而眠者始帖席矣；司戶之貶一行，而市井皆相賀焉。脫距之詩作，而庶民歌於道；拔釘之謡徵，而士論快於朝。「吾今召君」，似知其賢；「天下必肥」，似知其忠。能用之乎？譽樹不已，知其佞矣；忌賢無比，知其奸矣。能去之乎？夫既往之迹，固歷歷可指，而維新之政，則蕩蕩難名。取於眾善之中，以匡一代之治，亦可以見諸生致用之學。
問：廣東為地，北距五嶺以達京國，南負重溟以受島夷，亦南陬一大都會也。自入我朝百二十年，仁漸義摩，遭逢列聖，化行俗美，無間十州。然覆盆之地，日月或遺其明，而吹律之谷，陽春尚有所待。
translation_en:
…trouble: upon whom, then, were the hopes of the people of Liao to rest? Why was the banishment of the Sanmiao undertaken so promptly upon the assumption of the regency? Why did the execution at the two gate towers occur so promptly upon the assumption of the acting chief ministership? Once the traitor to the state had received his due punishment, those who slept could at last rest securely on their mats; once the demotion to household administrator had been carried out, people in the markets congratulated one another. When the poem about removing the spurs was composed, the common people sang it along the roads; when the song about pulling out the nail found fulfillment, the scholars at court expressed their satisfaction. “I now summon you” seems to show recognition of his worth; “All under Heaven will surely prosper” seems to show recognition of his loyalty. But could such men actually be employed? His ceaseless praise of a tree revealed his sycophancy; his unparalleled jealousy of the worthy revealed his wickedness. But could such men actually be removed? The deeds of the past can indeed be pointed out distinctly, while the measures of our renewed government are so vast that they are difficult to describe. By selecting from these many good precedents to support the governance of an age, you students may also demonstrate the practical application of your learning.
Question: Guangdong extends northward to the Five Ridges, through which it reaches the imperial capital, and has the vast seas at its southern back, receiving the island peoples. It is thus a great center of convergence in the southern reaches. In the hundred and twenty years since it came under our dynasty, it has been steeped in benevolence and shaped by righteousness. Under successive sage emperors, moral transformation has spread and customs have improved throughout its ten prefectures. Yet there may be places like the space beneath an overturned basin, which the light of sun and moon fails to reach; and valleys where pitch pipes are blown still await the warmth of spring…

title: 弘治二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
是以於此不能無言焉夫海濱鄒魯
前志豈溢美哉是教化未嘗不明也
然而深山大谷之中桀驁自雄者或
尚昧於逆順披猖相扇者或樂趨於
逋逃伊欲人皆知學盡如昌黎之時
其民知義盡如東坡之說其道何由
中州典禮前志豈過情哉是風俗未
嘗不美也然而遐陬僻壤之地人不
巾屨尚俎豆之足言鄉無詩書惟巫
===
鬼之是事伊欲衣冠相尚盡如圖經
之言華風可觀盡如廣平之治其術
安在桴鼓不鳴久矣無盜賊之虞也
然而三五鼠輩偶出入於近地一二
狗偷尚竊伏於水鄉弭之之策誠不
可忽夫化盜為民固前輩之盛德以
盜捕盜亦前輩之良規施之於今二
者將孰宜烽燧無煙久矣無蠻夷之
患也然而高凉之衆時或駭於鳥驚
punctuated: 是以於此不能無言焉。夫「海濱鄒魯」，前志豈溢美哉？是教化未嘗不明也。然而深山大谷之中，桀驁自雄者或尚昧於逆順，披猖相扇者或樂趨於逋逃。伊欲人皆知學，盡如昌黎之時，其民知義，盡如東坡之說，其道何由？「中州典禮」，前志豈過情哉？是風俗未嘗不美也。然而遐陬僻壤之地，人不巾屨，尚俎豆之足言？鄉無詩書，惟巫鬼之是事。伊欲衣冠相尚，盡如圖經之言，華風可觀，盡如廣平之治，其術安在？桴鼓不鳴久矣，無盜賊之虞也。然而三五鼠輩偶出入於近地，一二狗偷尚竊伏於水鄉，弭之之策誠不可忽。夫化盜為民，固前輩之盛德；以盜捕盜，亦前輩之良規。施之於今，二者將孰宜？烽燧無煙久矣，無蠻夷之患也。然而高凉之衆時或駭於鳥驚
translation_en: For this reason, something must be said here. When earlier gazetteers called this region “Zou and Lu by the sea,” could that have been excessive praise? Its moral instruction has certainly not lacked clarity. Yet among the deep mountains and great valleys, some unruly men who assert their own power still fail to distinguish rebellion from obedience, while others incite one another to lawlessness and willingly take to flight as fugitives. If we wish everyone to value learning, just as in Changli’s time, and all the people to understand righteousness, just as Dongpo described, by what means can this be achieved? When earlier gazetteers spoke of “the rites and ceremonies of the Central Plains,” could they have exaggerated? The customs have certainly not lacked excellence. Yet in remote and secluded places, people wear neither proper headcloths nor shoes—what is there to say of their observance of sacrificial rites [?]? Villages lack the Odes and Documents and attend only to shamans and spirits. If we wish people to esteem proper caps and robes, just as the Illustrated Gazetteer describes, and to display admirable Chinese customs, just as under Guangping’s administration, what methods will achieve this? The alarm drums have long been silent: there has been no fear of bandits. Yet a handful of ratlike scoundrels occasionally come and go nearby, and one or two doglike thieves still lurk secretly in the waterside settlements. Plans to suppress them must certainly not be neglected. Transforming bandits into ordinary subjects was indeed a great achievement of our predecessors’ virtue; employing bandits to capture bandits was also a sound measure devised by our predecessors. Which of these two would be appropriate to apply today? The beacon fires have long sent up no smoke: there has been no trouble from the Man and Yi peoples. Yet the people of Gaoliang are still sometimes thrown into alarm like startled birds…

title: 弘治二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
瀧水之徒尚未解於烏合制之之道
誠不可緩夫高其城垣威以刑法固
禦夷之術統以渠率粗定綱紀亦治
夷之法施之於今二者為孰得諸生
生長是邦籌之熟矣革其陋而歸之
華去其敝而歸之治必有可行之道
其明言之用採以為時政之助
punctuated: 瀧水之徒尚未解於烏合，制之之道誠不可緩。夫高其城垣，威以刑法，固禦夷之術；統以渠率，粗定綱紀，亦治夷之法。施之於今，二者為孰得？諸生生長是邦，籌之熟矣。革其陋而歸之華，去其敝而歸之治，必有可行之道。其明言之，用採以為時政之助。
translation_en: …the bands in Shuangshui have still not dispersed their motley gatherings. Measures to bring them under control truly brook no delay. Raising the city walls and overawing them with penal law is certainly a means of holding the non-Han peoples at bay; placing them under their own chieftains and establishing a rudimentary framework of discipline is also a method of governing them. Applied today, which of these two approaches would be more appropriate? You candidates were born and raised in this region and have considered these matters thoroughly. There must be practicable means of reforming its crude customs and bringing it into the Chinese cultural fold, eliminating its abuses and bringing it to good order. Explain these clearly, so that your proposals may be adopted to assist the governance of the day.

title: 弘治二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
君子上達
區元廣
同考試官學正章批此題反天理與知行本是註
釋作者乃舍此而他求之何哉淨而暢整而不冗
則有此篇况餘作稱是多士之冠無以易子矣
考試官教諭周批詞達題意
考試官教諭吳批發出上達之意可嘉
===
君子惟所循者正故所造者遠甚矣君子之所
以異於人也所循既正所造有不遠哉昔吾夫
子之意若曰天之生人不能以皆同人之爲人
宜有以自異有君子焉知吾心之理有以壞於
欲也於是思有以復之居必於仁由必於義而
所居所由不敢一入於不善之區知吾性之天
有以奪於人也於是思有以還之非法不言非
道不行而一言一行不敢一置於有過之地動
焉如是靜焉如是不以動靜而或殊暫焉如是
punctuated:
第壹塲
四書
「君子上達」
區元廣

同考試官學正章批：「此題反天理與知行，本是註釋，作者乃舍此而他求之，何哉？淨而暢，整而不冗，則有此篇。况餘作稱是，多士之冠，無以易子矣。」
考試官教諭周批：「詞達題意。」
考試官教諭吳批：「發出上達之意，可嘉。」

君子惟所循者正，故所造者遠。甚矣，君子之所以異於人也！所循既正，所造有不遠哉？昔吾夫子之意若曰：天之生人，不能以皆同；人之爲人，宜有以自異。有君子焉，知吾心之理有以壞於欲也，於是思有以復之。居必於仁，由必於義，而所居所由，不敢一入於不善之區。知吾性之天有以奪於人也，於是思有以還之。非法不言，非道不行，而一言一行，不敢一置於有過之地。動焉如是，靜焉如是，不以動靜而或殊；暫焉如是
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books
“The gentleman advances upward”
Ou Yuanguang

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, an Instructor: “For this topic, returning to heavenly principle, together with knowing and acting, is already explained in the commentary. Why, then, does the author set this aside and seek elsewhere? Yet here is an essay that is clean and fluent, orderly without being wordy. Moreover, his other compositions are of comparable quality. As foremost among the candidates, you cannot be displaced.”
Comment by Examiner Zhou, an Instructor: “The wording conveys the meaning of the topic.”
Comment by Examiner Wu, an Instructor: “It brings out the meaning of advancing upward: commendable.”

It is precisely because what the gentleman follows is correct that what he attains is far-reaching. How great is that which distinguishes the gentleman from other people! Since what he follows is correct, could his attainment fail to be far-reaching? The meaning of our Master’s words of old was as if he had said: When Heaven brings people into being, it cannot make them all alike; as human beings, people should have some means of distinguishing themselves. There is a gentleman who recognizes that the principle within his own heart has been damaged by desire, and therefore considers how to restore it. He invariably dwells in benevolence and proceeds by righteousness; in where he dwells and the path he follows, he dares not once enter the realm of what is not good. He recognizes that what is heavenly in his nature has been usurped by what is human, and therefore considers how to recover it. He says nothing that does not accord with proper standards and does nothing that does not accord with the Way. In every word and every deed, he dares not once place himself where there is fault. He is thus in activity and thus in stillness, never differing on account of activity or stillness; he is thus for a brief time…

title: 弘治二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
久焉如是不以久暫而有異其反天理也如此
殆見吾之所知者日累一日自然貫穿漸漸乎
入於高明之域萬境圓融一天理之充周也吾
之所行者日積一日自然成熟駸駸乎至於高
明之所八荒洞達一天道之流行也欲盡而理
還譬之陟遐不自知其至於遠矣人泯而天定
譬之升髙不自知其至於巔矣其日進於高明
也又如此噫君子之所存既異於人故其所至
亦異於人欲為君子者宜於是求焉大抵君子
===
小人如陰陽晝夜之不同然聖人之心嘗扶君
子而抑小人故履霜之戒惟恐陰之漸盛閉關
之謹惟恐陽之不長扶陽抑陰之意無往不在
而人不皆為君子抑獨何哉然欲為君子豈有
他道亦曰為仁由己而已
仲尼祖述堯舜憲章文武上律天時下襲
水土辟如天地之無不持載無不覆
幬辟如四時之錯行如日月之代明
陳文輔
punctuated:
久焉如是，不以久暫而有異。其反天理也如此，殆見吾之所知者日累一日，自然貫穿，漸漸乎入於高明之域，萬境圓融，一天理之充周也；吾之所行者日積一日，自然成熟，駸駸乎至於高明之所，八荒洞達，一天道之流行也。欲盡而理還，譬之陟遐，不自知其至於遠矣；人泯而天定，譬之升髙，不自知其至於巔矣。其日進於高明也又如此。噫！君子之所存既異於人，故其所至亦異於人。欲為君子者，宜於是求焉。大抵君子、小人，如陰陽晝夜之不同。然聖人之心嘗扶君子而抑小人，故履霜之戒，惟恐陰之漸盛；閉關之謹，惟恐陽之不長。扶陽抑陰之意，無往不在，而人不皆為君子，抑獨何哉？然欲為君子，豈有他道？亦曰為仁由己而已。

仲尼祖述堯舜，憲章文武，上律天時，下襲水土。辟如天地之無不持載，無不覆幬；辟如四時之錯行，如日月之代明。

陳文輔
translation_en:
…and remains so over a long time, making no distinction between long and short durations. Such is his return to Heaven’s principle. We may then see that what he knows accumulates day after day and naturally becomes interconnected, gradually entering the realm of loftiness and illumination. The myriad circumstances are harmoniously integrated: the single principle of Heaven pervades them all. What he puts into practice accumulates day after day and naturally matures, steadily advancing toward loftiness and illumination. The eight farthest regions are open and unobstructed: the single Way of Heaven flows through them all. When desire is exhausted and principle restored, it is like journeying afar, reaching a distant place without realizing it. When human impulses subside and Heaven’s endowment becomes settled, it is like climbing a height, reaching the summit without realizing it. Such, too, is his daily progress toward loftiness and illumination. Ah! Since what the gentleman preserves within himself differs from that of other people, what he attains also differs. Those who wish to become gentlemen should seek it here. In general, gentlemen and petty men differ as yin and yang, day and night differ. Yet the sage’s heart has ever upheld gentlemen and restrained petty men. Thus the warning about treading on frost expresses his fear that yin will gradually become powerful; his care in closing the passes expresses his fear that yang will fail to grow. The intention to uphold yang and restrain yin is present everywhere. Why, then, do people not all become gentlemen? Yet can there be any other way to become a gentleman? It is simply this: the practice of benevolence depends on oneself.

Zhongni transmitted the traditions of Yao and Shun and took Kings Wen and Wu as his models. Above, he followed the seasons of Heaven; below, he conformed to the waters and the land. He was like Heaven and Earth, which support and bear all things and shelter and cover all things; like the four seasons proceeding in succession; and like the sun and moon shining in turn.

Chen Wenfu

title: 弘治二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
同考試官訓導劉批〔此題內外本末不可不就聖人身上說就聖人身上說不謂之德謂之何哉明白整齊無如也作〕
同考試官教諭柯批〔此文一氣呵成畧無凝滯〕
考試官教諭周批〔詞旨俱優允宜錄出〕
考試官教諭吳批〔體認眞切〕
論聖□德之全一造化之妙蓋聖人天地一而已
矣然則吾夫子之德非天地之道又何足以擬
之哉中庸論天道至此若謂道莫大於堯舜仲
尼則遠宗其道而不遺法莫備於文武仲尼則
===
近守其法而不失合帝王而一之內外本末無
不周備矣天道有四時仲尼則上法其自然之
運水土有四方仲尼則下因其一定之理合天
地而一之內外本末無有虧欠矣辟之天地焉
博也厚也舉萬物皆在持載之中高也明也合
萬物皆在覆幬之下仲尼之德內外本末兼載
無不盡包括無或遺何以異於是辟之四時日
月焉四時迭用二氣運行而不窮日月互明萬
古流行而不息仲尼之德內外本末前不見其
punctuated:
同考試官訓導劉批〔此題內外本末，不可不就聖人身上說。就聖人身上說，不謂之德，謂之何哉？明白整齊，無如也作。〕
同考試官教諭柯批〔此文一氣呵成，畧無凝滯。〕
考試官教諭周批〔詞旨俱優，允宜錄出。〕
考試官教諭吳批〔體認眞切。〕
論聖□德之全，一造化之妙。蓋聖人、天地，一而已矣。然則吾夫子之德，非天地之道，又何足以擬之哉？中庸論天道至此，若謂道莫大於堯舜，仲尼則遠宗其道而不遺；法莫備於文武，仲尼則近守其法而不失。合帝王而一之，內外本末，無不周備矣。天道有四時，仲尼則上法其自然之運；水土有四方，仲尼則下因其一定之理。合天地而一之，內外本末，無有虧欠矣。辟之天地焉，博也，厚也，舉萬物皆在持載之中；高也，明也，合萬物皆在覆幬之下。仲尼之德，內外本末，兼載無不盡，包括無或遺，何以異於是？辟之四時日月焉，四時迭用，二氣運行而不窮；日月互明，萬古流行而不息。仲尼之德，內外本末，前不見其

Associate Examiner Liu, an Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔In this topic, the inward and outward aspects, the roots and branches, must all be discussed in relation to the sage himself. When discussed in relation to the sage himself, what could they be called but virtue? For clarity and orderly presentation, no composition equals this [?].〕
Associate Examiner Ke, an Instructor, comments: 〔This essay flows in a single breath, without the slightest impediment.〕
Examiner Zhou, an Instructor, comments: 〔Both wording and purport are excellent. It certainly merits inclusion in the record.〕
Examiner Wu, an Instructor, comments: 〔The understanding is true and penetrating.〕
To discuss the completeness of the sage’s virtue [one character illegible] is to unite it with the wondrous workings of creation. For the sage and Heaven and Earth are simply one. What, then, other than the Way of Heaven and Earth could adequately serve as a comparison for our Master’s virtue? At this point in its discussion of the Way of Heaven, the Doctrine of the Mean seems to say: no Way is greater than that of Yao and Shun, and Zhongni follows their Way from distant antiquity, omitting nothing; no institutions are more complete than those of Wen and Wu, and Zhongni preserves their institutions from more recent times, losing nothing. He brings the emperors and kings together into a unity, complete in every inward and outward aspect, root and branch. The Way of Heaven has its four seasons, and Zhongni models himself above on their spontaneous revolutions; waters and lands have their four quarters, and Zhongni conforms below to their fixed principles. He brings Heaven and Earth together into a unity, lacking nothing in any inward or outward aspect, root or branch.
Compare him to Heaven and Earth: in their breadth and depth, all things are sustained and borne; in their height and brightness, all things lie beneath their sheltering canopy. Zhongni’s virtue, in its inward and outward aspects, roots and branches, bears everything fully and embraces everything without omission. How does it differ from this? Compare him to the four seasons and the sun and moon: the four seasons take their turns, and the two vital forces circulate without exhaustion; the sun and moon shine in alternation, moving through all ages without ceasing. title: 弘治二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
有始後不見其有終何以異於是吁不觀天地
之道無以見聖人之德然非吾夫子又何足以
當之此吾夫子所以盡中庸之道而為聖之時
歟大抵中庸一書子思子為道統而作故其歷
敘大舜文武周公而必繼以孔子之言歷言天
道人道得時措之宜垂萬世之法而必繼以孔
子之事於以見孔子為道德之宗主古今帝王
之師也夫豈春秋一孔子哉
諸侯朝於天子曰述職述職者述所職也
===
何文華
考試官教諭周批題本揭書出若此題者亦
明白平易但作者於述所職處多涉入巡守事
敷暢而有條為予起敬
考試官教諭吳批以考禮正刑立說深得先
王述職之意一結尤見學識
論下之朝上有其名而有其義焉蓋朝覲者臣
之所以尊君也然亦豈無事而空行哉晏子舉
以告景公而孟子述以為宣王告宜也且天下
punctuated:
有始，後不見其有終，何以異於是？吁！不觀天地之道，無以見聖人之德；然非吾夫子，又何足以當之？此吾夫子所以盡中庸之道而為聖之時歟！大抵《中庸》一書，子思子為道統而作，故其歷敘大舜、文、武、周公，而必繼以孔子之言；歷言天道、人道，得時措之宜，垂萬世之法，而必繼以孔子之事。於以見孔子為道德之宗主、古今帝王之師也。夫豈春秋一孔子哉！
諸侯朝於天子曰述職，述職者述所職也。
何文華
考試官教諭周批：題本揭書出，若此題者亦明白平易。但作者於述所職處，多涉入巡守事，敷暢而有條，為予起敬。
考試官教諭吳批：以考禮正刑立說，深得先王述職之意，一結尤見學識。
論下之朝上，有其名而有其義焉。蓋朝覲者，臣之所以尊君也，然亦豈無事而空行哉？晏子舉以告景公，而孟子述以為宣王告，宜也。且天下
translation_en:
…a beginning, nor, looking forward, can one see its end: how does this differ from those things? Ah! Without observing the Way of Heaven and Earth, one cannot perceive the virtue of the sage. Yet who but our Master could measure up to it? Is this not how our Master fully realized the Way of the Mean and became the sage who acted according to the times? Broadly speaking, Master Zisi composed the Doctrine of the Mean for the sake of the transmission of the Way. Thus, when he successively recounts the deeds of the great Shun, Kings Wen and Wu, and the Duke of Zhou, he invariably follows them with the words of Confucius. When he discusses in turn the Way of Heaven and the Way of humanity, their application as circumstances require, and the standards they bequeath to all generations, he invariably follows these with the deeds of Confucius. Here we see that Confucius is the supreme authority in the Way and virtue, and the teacher of emperors and kings, ancient and modern. Could he be merely one Confucius of the Spring and Autumn period?
“When the feudal lords attend court before the Son of Heaven, this is called ‘reporting on their duties.’ Reporting on their duties means reporting on the responsibilities entrusted to them.”
He Wenhua
Comment by Examiner Zhou, Instructor: “The topic is drawn directly from the book [?]; a topic such as this is also clear and straightforward. However, in discussing ‘reporting on the responsibilities entrusted to them,’ the author frequently brings in matters concerning the sovereign’s inspection tours. His exposition is expansive and orderly, inspiring my respect.”
Comment by Examiner Wu, Instructor: “By grounding his argument in examining ritual observance and rectifying punishments, he has deeply grasped the former kings’ intent in requiring reports on duties. The conclusion particularly reveals his learning and discernment.”
To discuss the attendance of inferiors at the court of their superior: it has both a designation and a meaning. Court audiences are the means by which ministers honor their ruler. Yet could they be performed emptily, with no business to transact? Yanzi invoked this to instruct Duke Jing, and Mencius recounted it to instruct King Xuan: fittingly so. Moreover, all under Heaven…

title: 弘治二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
國家非一人所能以獨理於是有封建之法焉
四方萬國非一統不可以言治於是有朝覲之
典焉是故列爵惟五小大不同均之為諸侯也
雖各有土地然六年一覲於天子之庭者無小
大也分土惟三遠近不一均之為侯國也雖各
有人民然六載一朝於天子之堂者無遠近也
其為此舉豈無謂哉曰述職而已謂之述職又
何謂歟其必封國之始所受於天子其大者有
禮焉今則以所受之禮敷奏於朝廷之上使得
===
以考其違僭而禮樂自天子出矣建邦之初所
受於天子其大者又有刑焉今則以所受之刑
條陳於殿陛之下使得以正其偏枉而征伐自
天子出矣此則所謂述所職也晏子之告景公
如此景公果能行之則觀於轉附以至琅邪又
何以異於先王觀哉孟子述以為宣王告則雪
宮之樂又豈得不與民同邪嘗觀古昔盛時諸
侯之述職也既如此然天子亦以時巡狩焉當
其往来之頃慶讓黜陟纖悉具備夫豈無事而
punctuated: 國家非一人所能以獨理，於是有封建之法焉。四方萬國非一統不可以言治，於是有朝覲之典焉。是故列爵惟五，小大不同，均之為諸侯也。雖各有土地，然六年一覲於天子之庭者，無小大也。分土惟三，遠近不一，均之為侯國也。雖各有人民，然六載一朝於天子之堂者，無遠近也。其為此舉，豈無謂哉？曰：述職而已。謂之述職，又何謂歟？其必封國之始所受於天子，其大者有禮焉。今則以所受之禮敷奏於朝廷之上，使得以考其違僭，而禮樂自天子出矣。建邦之初所受於天子，其大者又有刑焉。今則以所受之刑條陳於殿陛之下，使得以正其偏枉，而征伐自天子出矣。此則所謂述所職也。晏子之告景公如此，景公果能行之，則觀於轉附以至琅邪，又何以異於先王觀哉？孟子述以為宣王告，則雪宮之樂又豈得不與民同邪？嘗觀古昔盛時諸侯之述職也，既如此，然天子亦以時巡狩焉。當其往来之頃，慶讓黜陟，纖悉具備，夫豈無事而
translation_en:
…the state cannot be governed by one person alone; hence the system of establishing enfeoffed domains. The myriad states in the four quarters cannot be considered well governed unless united under a single authority; hence the institution of court audiences. Thus, although the five ranks of nobility differ in standing, all their holders are feudal lords. Each possesses his own territory, yet all appear once every six years in the Son of Heaven’s court, regardless of rank. Although the three grades of territorial allotment differ in their distance from the royal court, all are feudal states. Each has its own people, yet all attend an audience once every six years in the Son of Heaven’s hall, regardless of distance. Could this practice have no purpose? Its purpose is simply to report on the discharge of their duties. What, then, does such reporting mean?
Among the most important things received from the Son of Heaven when a domain was first enfeoffed were the rites. The lords now report fully before the court on the rites entrusted to them, enabling the sovereign to examine their violations and usurpations; thus rites and music issue from the Son of Heaven. Among the most important things received from the Son of Heaven when a state was first established were also the penal laws. The lords now present itemized reports below the palace steps on the penal laws entrusted to them, enabling the sovereign to correct their partiality and injustice; thus punitive expeditions issue from the Son of Heaven. This is what is meant by reporting on the discharge of one’s duties.
Such was Yanzi’s counsel to Duke Jing. Had Duke Jing truly put it into practice, how would his tour to Zhuanfu [?] and onward to Langye have differed from the tours of the former kings? Mengzi recounted this counsel to King Xuan: how, then, could the pleasures of the Snow Palace fail to be shared with the people? I have considered how, in the flourishing ages of antiquity, the feudal lords reported on their duties in this manner, while the Son of Heaven also undertook tours of inspection at the appointed times. During these journeys to and fro, rewards and reprimands, demotions and promotions were all attended to in the finest detail. How could they have had no business to conduct and…

title: 弘治二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
空行先王治天下之大法實不出此後世不此
之圖而乃區區於為治之末雖欲言治皆茍而
已有志於治者尚鑒於斯
易
先王以建萬國親諸侯
區元廣
同考試官學正章批此題本冠冕作者於建國
親侯處多不能以比天下立說殊失象傳之意此篇
獨有所見是宜錄出
===
考試官教諭周批能說出先王比民之意可取
考試官教諭吳批得象傳聖人之旨取之
先王體比之象而盡比天下之道焉盖建國親
侯先王所以比於天下而无間者也象易者有
見於此而著明之其旨深矣昔吾夫子傳比之
象盖謂地上有水比之象也先王觀象體義以
為水比於地不容有間君之於民容有間耶彼
天下之大統御乎我者非一人欲人人而比之
勢不能也必分茅胙土而萬國以建所謂百里
punctuated:
空行？先王治天下之大法，實不出此。後世不此之圖，而乃區區於為治之末，雖欲言治，皆茍而已有志於治者，尚鑒於斯。

易
先王以建萬國，親諸侯。
區元廣

同考試官學正章批：此題本冠冕，作者於建國親侯處，多不能以比天下立說，殊失象傳之意。此篇獨有所見，是宜錄出。

考試官教諭周批：能說出先王比民之意，可取。

考試官教諭吳批：得象傳聖人之旨，取之。

先王體比之象，而盡比天下之道焉。盖建國親侯，先王所以比於天下而无間者也。象易者有見於此而著明之，其旨深矣。昔吾夫子傳比之象，盖謂地上有水，比之象也。先王觀象體義，以為水比於地，不容有間；君之於民，容有間耶？彼天下之大，統御乎我者非一人，欲人人而比之，勢不能也。必分茅胙土，而萬國以建，所謂百里
translation_en:
…travel to no purpose? The great principles by which the former kings governed All under Heaven truly extended no further than this. Later generations failed to pursue this, instead busying themselves with the incidental details of government. Though they wished to speak of good government, their efforts were merely makeshift. Let those committed to good government take warning from this.

Book of Changes
“The former kings accordingly established the myriad states and drew the feudal lords close.”
By Ou Yuanguang.

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: This topic is inherently dignified. In discussing the establishment of states and the drawing close of the feudal lords, writers generally fail to ground their arguments in bringing All under Heaven into union, thus gravely missing the meaning of the Commentary on the Images. This essay alone shows insight; it deserves to be transcribed here.

Comment by Examiner Zhou, Instructor: It succeeds in articulating the former kings’ intention to unite with the people. Worth accepting.

Comment by Examiner Wu, Instructor: It grasps the sage’s intent in the Commentary on the Images. Accept it.

The former kings embodied the image of Union and fully realized the way of bringing All under Heaven into union. Establishing states and drawing the feudal lords close were the means by which the former kings united with All under Heaven without any separation. The author who expounded the images of the Changes perceived this and made it manifest. Profound indeed is its meaning!

Long ago, our Master transmitted an explanation of the image of Union, saying that water upon the earth is the image of Union. The former kings contemplated this image and embodied its meaning, reasoning that water lies close to the earth, permitting no separation: could separation be permitted between the ruler and his people? Across the vastness of All under Heaven, those under my rule are more than one person. To seek union with every individual is impossible under the circumstances. It is therefore necessary to distribute the thatch and confer lands, thereby establishing the myriad states, including those described as measuring one hundred li…

title: 弘治二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
者有焉七十里者有焉四海之廣仰戴乎我者
非一姓若人人而比之力不及也必經野畫地
而萬邦以立所謂五十里者有焉附庸者有焉
萬國建矣民猶與我懸絶也使不親諸侯以比
之奚可乎由是萬國之中有公也侯也我則托
之以心膂隆之以恩寵而親之之禮有加彼豈
不能達吾仁於天下是天下之民皆為吾之所
比矣萬邦立矣民猶與我阻隔也使不親侯國
以比之其可乎由是萬邦之內有伯也子男也
===
我則視之如手足待之以誠信而親之之意不
替彼豈不能沛吾恩於四海是四海之民皆為
吾之所比矣是則先王之於民曾何相間之有
乎抑論之地上有水君民合一之象故先王以
建國親侯地中有水兵農合一之象故君子以
容民畜眾蓋建國親侯封建法也于以之治國
容民畜眾井田法也于以之防虞合而觀之則
雖王者之政亦不出於此矣
是故君子所居而安者易之序也所樂而
punctuated:
者有焉，七十里者有焉。四海之廣，仰戴乎我者非一姓，若人人而比之，力不及也。必經野畫地，而萬邦以立，所謂五十里者有焉，附庸者有焉。萬國建矣，民猶與我懸絶也，使不親諸侯以比之，奚可乎？由是萬國之中，有公也、侯也，我則托之以心膂，隆之以恩寵，而親之之禮有加。彼豈不能達吾仁於天下？是天下之民皆為吾之所比矣。萬邦立矣，民猶與我阻隔也，使不親侯國以比之，其可乎？由是萬邦之內，有伯也、子男也，我則視之如手足，待之以誠信，而親之之意不替。彼豈不能沛吾恩於四海？是四海之民皆為吾之所比矣。是則先王之於民，曾何相間之有乎？抑論之，地上有水，君民合一之象，故先王以建國親侯；地中有水，兵農合一之象，故君子以容民畜眾。蓋建國親侯，封建法也，于以之治國；容民畜眾，井田法也，于以之防虞。合而觀之，則雖王者之政，亦不出於此矣。

是故君子所居而安者，易之序也；所樂而
translation_en:
…there are such domains, and there are those measuring seventy li. Throughout the vast expanse within the Four Seas, those who look up to me and acknowledge my rule belong to more than one clan. Were I to seek union with every person individually, my strength would not suffice. I must therefore lay out the countryside and demarcate the land, establishing the myriad domains: among them are those said to measure fifty li, and those that are dependencies.

Once the myriad states have been established, the people remain far removed from me. How could it be acceptable not to draw close to the feudal lords in order to unite with the people? Thus, among the myriad states there are dukes and marquises. I entrust them with responsibility as my heart and sinews, exalt them with favor and honor, and accord them ever greater ceremonial marks of intimacy. How could they fail to convey my benevolence throughout All-under-Heaven? In this way, all the people of All-under-Heaven are united with me. Once the myriad domains have been established, barriers still separate the people from me. How could it be acceptable not to draw close to the lordly states in order to unite with the people? Thus, within the myriad domains there are earls, viscounts, and barons. I regard them as my hands and feet, treat them with sincerity and trust, and never diminish my intention to draw close to them. How could they fail to spread my favor abundantly throughout the Four Seas? In this way, all the people within the Four Seas are united with me. What separation, then, could ever have existed between the former kings and their people?

To discuss this further: water upon the earth is the image of ruler and people united as one; thus the former kings established states and drew close to the feudal lords. Water within the earth is the image of soldiers and farmers united as one; thus the noble man embraces the people and nurtures the multitude. Establishing states and drawing close to the feudal lords constitutes the method of enfeoffment, by which to govern the realm. Embracing the people and nurturing the multitude constitutes the well-field method, by which to guard against unforeseen dangers. Viewed together, even the government of a true king does not go beyond these principles.

Therefore, what the noble man abides in and finds peace in is the sequence of the Changes; what he delights in and…

title: 弘治二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
玩者爻之辭也是故君子居則觀其
象而玩其辭動則觀其變而玩其占
是以自天祐之吉无不利
廖與
同考試官學正章批此題本是兩截而場中分截差
者甚多間有不差而措詞又傷於冗長此作文理俱穩
宜錄以為學者式
考試官教諭周批詞理平順錄之
考試官教諭吳批得大傳立言之旨可取
===
有君子身心學易之事有君子動靜學易之效
蓋易為君子謀也使身心學之而動靜或違焉
又豈能獲乎福哉昔吾夫子大傳言君子學易
之事蓋謂否泰剥復潜見飛躍易之序也君子
學易知其序之有常故於身之所處從容順適
而安舒自得者得非在於此乎吉凶悔吝貞利
无咎爻之辭也君子學易知其理之无窮故於
心之所樂沈潜反覆而玩習不舎者又豈外於
是乎君子身心之學易如此而其動靜之於易
punctuated:
玩者，爻之辭也。是故君子居則觀其象而玩其辭，動則觀其變而玩其占。是以自天祐之，吉无不利。

廖與

同考試官學正章批：此題本是兩截，而場中分截差者甚多，間有不差，而措詞又傷於冗長。此作文理俱穩，宜錄以為學者式。

考試官教諭周批：詞理平順，錄之。

考試官教諭吳批：得大傳立言之旨，可取。

有君子身心學易之事，有君子動靜學易之效。蓋易為君子謀也，使身心學之而動靜或違焉，又豈能獲乎福哉？昔吾夫子大傳言君子學易之事，蓋謂否泰剥復、潜見飛躍，易之序也。君子學易，知其序之有常，故於身之所處，從容順適而安舒自得者，得非在於此乎？吉凶悔吝、貞利无咎，爻之辭也。君子學易，知其理之无窮，故於心之所樂，沈潜反覆而玩習不舎者，又豈外於是乎？君子身心之學易如此，而其動靜之於易
translation_en:
…what he ponders with delight are the statements attached to the lines. Thus, when at rest, the gentleman observes its images and ponders its statements; when acting, he observes its changes and ponders its prognostications. Therefore, Heaven assists him: good fortune, with nothing unfavorable.

Liao Yu 廖與

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, School Instructor: This topic consists of two distinct sections, yet very many candidates in the examination divided them incorrectly. Among the occasional answers that divided them correctly, the wording nevertheless suffered from excessive length. This composition is sound in both writing and reasoning and should be recorded as a model for students.

Comment by Examiner Zhou, Instructor: The wording and reasoning are clear and smooth. Record it.

Comment by Examiner Wu, Instructor: It grasps the intent behind the statements of the Great Commentary. It merits acceptance.

There is the gentleman’s practice of studying the Changes in body and mind, and there is the efficacy of his study of the Changes in action and repose. The Changes provides counsel for the gentleman. If he studies it in body and mind but sometimes departs from it in action or repose, how could he obtain blessings?

Formerly, our Master spoke in the Great Commentary of the gentleman’s practice of studying the Changes. His meaning was that Obstruction and Peace, Stripping Away and Return, and hiding, appearing, flying, and leaping constitute the sequence of the Changes. In studying the Changes, the gentleman knows that its sequence has a constant order. Thus, wherever he finds himself, he accommodates himself calmly and appropriately, remaining at ease and content. Is this not grounded in that sequence?

Good fortune and misfortune, regret and humiliation, constancy, benefit, and freedom from blame are the statements attached to the lines. In studying the Changes, the gentleman knows that its principles are inexhaustible. Thus, in what delights his mind, he immerses himself deeply, returning to it repeatedly, pondering and studying without cease. Could this lie outside those statements?

Such is the gentleman’s study of the Changes in body and mind; as for his action and repose in relation to the Changes…

title: 弘治二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
何如彼易有象而後有辭君子靜而學夫易也
旣觀夫得失憂虞之象矣又玩其吉凶悔吝之
辭焉筮有變而後有占君子動而學夫易也旣
觀夫剛柔進退之變矣又玩其所值吉凶之占
焉若然則一動一靜舉无違理是以自天祐之
而靜與吉會何所往而不利乎自天申之而動
與吉合何所適而不宜乎君子動靜之學易又
如此抑論之易為衆人作也而此獨以學易之
事歸之君子者蓋以易非聖人不能作非君子
===
莫能體故上文剛柔變化吉凶悔吝聖人作易
之事而此身心動靜无往非易君子學易之事
也吁易之為易聖人作之君子學之衆人棄焉
此傳易聖人所以不能不深有望於君子也
書
爾交脩予罔予棄予惟克邁乃訓說曰王
人求多聞時惟建事學于古訓乃有
獲事不師古以克永世匪說攸聞惟
學遜志務時敏厥脩乃來允懷于兹
punctuated:
何如？彼易有象而後有辭，君子靜而學夫易也，旣觀夫得失憂虞之象矣，又玩其吉凶悔吝之辭焉。筮有變而後有占，君子動而學夫易也，旣觀夫剛柔進退之變矣，又玩其所值吉凶之占焉。若然，則一動一靜，舉无違理。是以自天祐之，而靜與吉會，何所往而不利乎？自天申之，而動與吉合，何所適而不宜乎？君子動靜之學易又如此。抑論之，易為衆人作也，而此獨以學易之事歸之君子者，蓋以易非聖人不能作，非君子莫能體。故上文剛柔變化、吉凶悔吝，聖人作易之事；而此身心動靜，无往非易，君子學易之事也。吁！易之為易，聖人作之，君子學之，衆人棄焉。此傳易聖人所以不能不深有望於君子也。

書

爾交脩予，罔予棄，予惟克邁乃訓。說曰：「王，人求多聞，時惟建事。學于古訓，乃有獲；事不師古，以克永世，匪說攸聞。惟學遜志，務時敏，厥脩乃來。允懷于兹，」
translation_en:
…how, then, do they accord with the Changes in activity and stillness? In the Changes, images precede the appended statements. When the gentleman studies the Changes in stillness, he observes the images of gain and loss, sorrow and anxiety, and also ponders their statements concerning good fortune and misfortune, regret and humiliation. In milfoil divination, changes precede prognostications. When the gentleman studies the Changes in activity, he observes the changes of the firm and yielding, advancing and retreating, and also ponders the prognostications of good fortune and misfortune that he encounters. If he does this, then in every activity and every moment of stillness he never departs from principle. Thus Heaven itself assists him, and in stillness he meets with good fortune: wherever he goes, how could anything fail to be beneficial? Heaven itself extends its aid to him [?], and in activity he accords with good fortune: wherever he turns, how could anything be unfitting? Such, too, is the gentleman’s study of the Changes in activity and stillness.

Consider further: the Changes was made for everyone. Yet here the study of the Changes is attributed exclusively to the gentleman because only a sage could compose it, and only a gentleman can embody it. Thus the preceding discussion of the transformations of the firm and yielding, good fortune and misfortune, regret and humiliation concerns the sage’s composition of the Changes. Here, by contrast, the discussion of body and mind, activity and stillness, in which nothing lies outside the Changes, concerns the gentleman’s study of it. Ah! Such is the Changes: the sage composes it, the gentleman studies it, and ordinary people cast it aside. This is why the sage who transmitted the Changes could not but place profound hopes in the gentleman.

Book of Documents

“You must cultivate me in every respect; do not abandon me. I shall indeed carry out your instructions.” Yue said: “O King, a person seeks extensive learning in order to accomplish undertakings. By studying ancient teachings, one gains understanding. That one could conduct affairs without taking antiquity as a model and yet perpetuate one’s rule for generations is something I, Yue, have never heard. In learning, make your intentions humble and strive always to be diligent; then self-cultivation will follow. Truly cherish this…”

title: 弘治二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
道積于厥躬惟斅學半念終始典于
學厥德脩罔覺監于先王成憲其永
無愆
何文華
考試官教諭周批此題本長作者難於該括不泛
則失之畧詞不繁而理自足者僅見此篇
考試官教諭吳批說命一題本論學進德之詞此
篇講貫明白敻異衆作是宜錄出
賢王求訓於臣自許以力行之功大臣納誨於
===
君必詳其為學之道夫學所以進德也大臣因
賢王求訓以輔德其可不詳進夫為學之說也
哉昔高宗命傅說之意若曰生質之美係乎天
聿脩其德在乎人故予之德有未至爾當以柔
濟剛左右規正以輔成之猶麴蘖之於酒醴可
也我之德有未善汝必以可濟否左右弼直以
輔𤆄之猶鹽梅之於和羹可也毋以行之惟艱
為予棄予惟克邁乃訓而不怠焉毋以學終罔
顯為我棄我惟祗服其訓而不忽焉夫高宗以
punctuated:
道積于厥躬。惟斅學半，念終始典于學，厥德脩罔覺。監于先王成憲，其永無愆。
何文華。
考試官教諭周批：此題本長，作者難於該括，不泛則失之畧。詞不繁而理自足者，僅見此篇。
考試官教諭吳批：《說命》一題，本論學進德之詞。此篇講貫明白，敻異衆作，是宜錄出。

title: 弘治二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
輔德望之臣而自許其力行矣傅説得不進其
為學之説哉於是稱之曰王以起其聽盖謂人
求多聞以資於人是惟立夫脩治之事然必學
于古訓以反諸巳斯可得乎脩治之理苟事不
師古而能長治久安豈説之所聞哉然其學也
必虛以受人遜其志如有所不能勤以勵已敏
於學如有所不及則脩治之理如泉始達源源
乎其來矣又必篤信乎此而不惑深念乎此而
勿忘則脩治之道有得於已又豈可以一二計
===
哉盖道積厥躬者體之立固學之半也而斅學
于人者用之行非學之半乎必兼體用而後聖
學可全也故始之自學終之教人一念終始常
在於學則脩治之德所造益深有不知其然而
然者矣夫德雖造於罔覺而法必監于先王盖
先王成法子孫之所當守者也于焉而是法之
則德脩於身而措之治天下又豈不要之永久
而無過舉也哉此為學之道高宗所宜自盡也
歟考之高宗得説以為相既以舟楫霖雨為喻
punctuated: 輔德望之臣，而自許其力行矣，傅説得不進其為學之説哉？於是稱之曰王，以起其聽，盖謂人求多聞以資於人，是惟立夫脩治之事；然必學于古訓以反諸巳，斯可得乎脩治之理。苟事不師古而能長治久安，豈説之所聞哉？然其學也，必虛以受人，遜其志如有所不能；勤以勵已，敏於學如有所不及，則脩治之理如泉始達，源源乎其來矣。又必篤信乎此而不惑，深念乎此而勿忘，則脩治之道有得於已，又豈可以一二計哉？盖道積厥躬者，體之立，固學之半也；而斅學于人者，用之行，非學之半乎？必兼體用而後聖學可全也。故始之自學，終之教人，一念終始常在於學，則脩治之德所造益深，有不知其然而然者矣。夫德雖造於罔覺，而法必監于先王，盖先王成法，子孫之所當守者也。于焉而是法之，則德脩於身而措之治天下，又豈不要之永久而無過舉也哉？此為學之道，高宗所宜自盡也歟？考之高宗得説以為相，既以舟楫霖雨為喻，
translation_en:
…looked to his minister to assist his virtue and pledged himself to put the teaching vigorously into practice. Could Fu Yue then fail to present his account of learning? Thus he addressed him as “King” to command his attention. His meaning was this: seeking extensive knowledge in order to draw upon others establishes only the practical work of self-cultivation and government. One must also study the teachings of antiquity and turn back upon oneself; only then can one grasp the principles of self-cultivation and government. If someone could achieve lasting order and enduring peace without taking antiquity as a model in his undertakings, would Yue ever have heard of such a thing?

In learning, one must empty oneself to receive instruction from others, humbling one’s mind as though there were things one could not accomplish; one must exert oneself diligently, applying oneself eagerly to learning as though unable to catch up. Then the principles of self-cultivation and government will flow forth continuously, like a spring first breaking through. One must also trust firmly in these principles without wavering, reflect deeply upon them, and never forget them. Then, having personally grasped the Way of self-cultivation and government, how could one’s gains be counted as merely one or two?

For the Way to accumulate within oneself is the establishment of its substance, and is certainly half of learning. To teach others is the exercise of its function: is this not the other half of learning? Only when substance and function are both embraced can the learning of the sages be complete. Thus one begins by learning oneself and ends by teaching others. If one’s mind remains constantly devoted to learning from beginning to end, one’s attainment in the virtue of self-cultivation and government will grow ever deeper, reaching a state that comes about without one’s knowing how it does so.

Although virtue may advance without conscious awareness, one must take the former kings as models for one’s standards. For the established institutions of the former kings are what their descendants ought to preserve. By modeling oneself upon these, one cultivates virtue in one’s own person and applies it to governing all under Heaven. How could this fail to aim at enduring success, free from mistaken actions? Is this not the Way of learning to which Gaozong ought to devote himself to the utmost? Examining how Gaozong obtained Yue as his chief minister, we find that he had already likened him to a boat and oars and to timely rain…

Other great principles, such as treating the Xia states as insiders and the Yi peoples as outsiders, and honoring kings while disparaging hegemons, number in the dozens. title: 弘治二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
於食焉自日之方中而至於日之昃終食之間
可少緩也文王之心有所為惟時汲汲而不暇
於食焉然一日之晷屢移而一食之養不暇文
王之心何心哉誠以多方之受非一民也寧無
未安者乎故欲推吾懷保之仁以及之使寒者
衣饑者食悉囿於春風和氣之中不啻懷保小
民而已方夏之撫非一姓也寧無不獲者乎故
必廣吾惠鮮之政以及之使老者安少者懷咸
樂於光天化日之下不但惠鮮鰥寡而已文王
===
心在乎民自不知其勤勞如此則無逸之實為
何如哉抑觀立政言罔攸兼于庶言庶獄庶慎
則文王又若無所事事者不讀無逸則無以知
文王之勤不讀立政則無以知文王之逸合二
書觀之則文王之所從事可知矣噫周公作書
以告成王一則欲其無逸以法乎先王一則欲
其任賢以登於至治周公忠愛之心何其至歟
詩
天子命我城彼朔方赫赫南仲玁狁于襄
punctuated:
於食焉。自日之方中而至於日之昃，終食之間，可少緩也。文王之心有所為，惟時汲汲而不暇於食焉。然一日之晷屢移，而一食之養不暇，文王之心何心哉？誠以多方之受非一民也，寧無未安者乎？故欲推吾懷保之仁以及之，使寒者衣，饑者食，悉囿於春風和氣之中，不啻懷保小民而已。方夏之撫非一姓也，寧無不獲者乎？故必廣吾惠鮮之政以及之，使老者安，少者懷，咸樂於光天化日之下，不但惠鮮鰥寡而已。文王心在乎民，自不知其勤勞如此，則無逸之實為何如哉？抑觀《立政》言「罔攸兼于庶言、庶獄、庶慎」，則文王又若無所事事者。不讀《無逸》，則無以知文王之勤；不讀《立政》，則無以知文王之逸。合二書觀之，則文王之所從事可知矣。噫！周公作書以告成王，一則欲其無逸以法乎先王，一則欲其任賢以登於至治。周公忠愛之心，何其至歟！

詩
天子命我，城彼朔方。赫赫南仲，玁狁于襄。
translation_en:
…to eat. From the sun’s reaching midday until its decline, he might have relaxed briefly for the time needed to finish a meal. Yet King Wen had a purpose at heart: he pressed urgently onward, finding no leisure to eat. The shadow marking the hours shifted repeatedly in a single day, yet he had no leisure for the nourishment of even one meal. What manner of heart was King Wen’s? Truly, those received under his rule from the many regions [?] were not just a single people: could any still lack security? Thus he wished to extend his benevolence in cherishing and protecting them, clothing the cold and feeding the hungry, enclosing all within the gentle warmth of a spring breeze. This went beyond merely cherishing and protecting the common people. Those he nurtured throughout the Chinese lands were not just a single clan: could any still lack their due? Thus he had to broaden his policies of kindness and relief to reach them, bringing peace to the old and affectionate care to the young, so that all might rejoice beneath the bright sky and the sun of transforming rule. This went beyond merely showing kindness and relief to widowers and widows. King Wen’s heart was set upon the people, and he himself was unaware that his labors were so great. How fully, then, did he embody freedom from idle ease!

Yet consider the statement in Establishing Government (Li zheng): “He did not concurrently concern himself with the various deliberations, legal cases, and matters requiring care.” King Wen then seems, again, to have had nothing to do. Without reading Against Idle Ease (Wu yi), one cannot understand King Wen’s diligence; without reading Establishing Government, one cannot understand his ease. Read these two texts together, and one can understand what King Wen devoted himself to. Ah! The Duke of Zhou composed these texts to admonish King Cheng. In one, he wished him to shun idle ease and model himself upon the former kings; in the other, he wished him to employ the worthy and attain perfect governance. How profound was the Duke of Zhou’s loyal affection!

text:

其入寇之心尚足慮哉聞南仲之受知於天子

===
