以先王亦以禽獸待之而唯謹於自治而已後
世不此之圖而乃務勤遠畧不亦惑之甚哉顧
punctuated: 命我以爾三軍往城于彼，庶乎防禦之有地也。盖以華制夷，莫先於城郭，而設險自固，實利於國家。戎行之意，其在茲乎？傳命令衆如此，但見當時之人知天子之倚重於南仲也如是，由是自將改觀，而南仲之聲威益振，赫然動人矣。玁狁雖在絕幕，行且知之，况城守有地，自有以奪其入寇之心，尚足慮哉？聞南仲之受知於天子也若此，由是自將起畏，而南仲之氣焰益增，赫然動衆矣。玁狁雖在絕域，行且聞之，况邊備正脩，自有以破其内侵之謀，尚足患哉？王庭不南，疆圉以之而晏然；牧馬自北，邊地為之而恬若。然則玁狁之襄，謂不在於朔方之城而可乎？吁！守内地以自固，致外患之自除，禦戎之道，尚孰有加於此哉？嗟夫！先王之待夷狄，其所以自治者嘗密，而所以治之者嘗疎，是何也？盖夷狄譬之禽獸然，惟力是恃，尚何是非曲直之足言？是以先王亦以禽獸待之，而唯謹於自治而已。後世不此之圖，而乃務勤遠畧，不亦惑之甚哉？顧
translation_en: …he therefore commanded me to take your three armies and build fortifications there, so that there might be a place from which to defend against them. For using the Chinese realm to restrain the barbarians, nothing takes precedence over fortified walls; establishing defensive barriers to secure oneself truly benefits the state. Was this not the purpose of the military expedition? Such was the command transmitted to the troops. We see that the people of that time, knowing how heavily the Son of Heaven relied upon Nan Zhong, would naturally come to regard him differently. Nan Zhong’s prestige and might thus grew still greater, striking awe into people. Though the Xianyun were beyond the desert, they would soon learn of it. Moreover, with a fortified position to hold, there would naturally be a means of robbing them of the will to raid. What further cause for anxiety could there be? Hearing how Nan Zhong enjoyed the Son of Heaven’s recognition, people would naturally begin to fear him. His imposing force would grow still greater, striking awe into the multitude. Though the Xianyun were in remote lands, they would soon hear of it. Moreover, with the frontier defenses being put in good order, there would naturally be a means of thwarting their plans to invade. What further cause for concern could there be? Their royal encampment would not move south, and the frontier would thereby be at peace; their horses would graze in the north [?], and the borderlands would thereby remain tranquil. Could one then say that the repulse of the Xianyun did not depend upon the fortification of Shuofang? Ah! To defend the inner territory and secure oneself, thereby causing external threats to disappear of themselves—what method of resisting the Rong could surpass this? Alas! In dealing with the Yi and Di, the former kings were always meticulous in ordering their own realm, but less exacting in governing those peoples. Why was this? The Yi and Di were comparable to birds and beasts, relying solely upon force: what point was there in speaking of right and wrong, justice and injustice? Thus the former kings likewise treated them as birds and beasts, merely taking care to put their own realm in order. Later generations failed to pursue this course and instead devoted their energies to distant conquests. Was this not delusion in the extreme? Yet…

title: 弘治二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
治之君尚其鑒之
以篤于周祜以對于天下
梁景行
同考試官訓導劉批此題學者於對天下猶能言
至篤周祜則多為所窘明而暢如此篇者何可多得哉
同考試官教諭柯批大雅題最平易作者却多以
對天下為篤周祜又或於篤周祜處以密人不恭講對
天下處以侵阮徂共講昔橫渠謂求詩者貴平易不
要崎嶇求合近時學者多坐此病正大鄭重無如此作
===
考試官教諭周批此正是作大雅義者
考試官教諭吳批作者俱知為伐密但少體貼親
切如此篇者
隆國祚而荅人心此聖人之伐罪然也盖文王
之心一天理之所在也其伐密也不過欲厚周
祜而荅天下耳豈私怒哉詩人述文王伐密之
意若曰小國不恭大邦是耻疆埸多事豈國家
之福哉故我文王之伐密也不過欲取彼兇殘
使宗廟無震驚之憂遏其寇亂使社稷無杌隉
punctuated:
治之君尚其鑒之！

「以篤于周祜，以對于天下。」
梁景行

同考試官訓導劉批：此題，學者於對天下猶能言，至篤周祜，則多為所窘。明而暢如此篇者，何可多得哉！

同考試官教諭柯批：大雅題最平易，作者却多以對天下為篤周祜，又或於篤周祜處以密人不恭講，對天下處以侵阮徂共講。昔橫渠謂求詩者貴平易，不要崎嶇求合。近時學者多坐此病，正大鄭重，無如此作。

考試官教諭周批：此正是作大雅義者。

考試官教諭吳批：作者俱知為伐密，但少體貼親切如此篇者。

隆國祚而荅人心，此聖人之伐罪然也。盖文王之心，一天理之所在也。其伐密也，不過欲厚周祜而荅天下耳，豈私怒哉？詩人述文王伐密之意，若曰：小國不恭，大邦是耻；疆埸多事，豈國家之福哉？故我文王之伐密也，不過欲取彼兇殘，使宗廟無震驚之憂；遏其寇亂，使社稷無杌隉
translation_en:
…may the ruler who governs take warning from this!

“To deepen the blessings of Zhou and to answer the expectations of all under Heaven.”
Liang Jingxing

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Assistant Instructor: On this topic, students can still find something to say about answering the expectations of all under Heaven, but most are at a loss when they reach deepening the blessings of Zhou. How often can one find an essay as clear and fluent as this?

Comment by Associate Examiner Ke, Instructor: Topics from the Greater Odes are perfectly straightforward, yet writers often treat answering the expectations of all under Heaven as equivalent to deepening the blessings of Zhou. Others explain deepening Zhou’s blessings through the people of Mi’s lack of respect, and answering the expectations of all under Heaven through their invasion of Ruan and advance upon Gong. Hengqu once said that those seeking to understand the Odes should prize simplicity and ease, rather than follow tortuous paths to force a correspondence. Students of recent times frequently fall into this fault. For uprightness, breadth, and gravity, no essay equals this one.

Comment by Examiner Zhou, Instructor: This is precisely how to compose an exposition on the Greater Odes.

Comment by Examiner Wu, Instructor: All the writers know that the passage concerns the campaign against Mi, but few enter into its meaning as closely and aptly as this essay does.

To prolong the dynasty’s good fortune and answer the people’s aspirations: such is the sage’s purpose in campaigning against the guilty. King Wen’s heart was wholly the abode of Heaven’s principle. In campaigning against Mi, he sought only to deepen Zhou’s blessings and answer the expectations of all under Heaven. Could it have been a matter of personal anger? In describing King Wen’s intention in campaigning against Mi, the poet seems to say: When a small state is disrespectful, the great state bears the shame. When troubles abound along the borders, how can this bring blessings to the state? Thus, when our King Wen campaigned against Mi, he sought only to seize those cruel and violent men, so that the ancestral temples would have no cause to fear alarm; to check their raids and disorder, so that the altars of soil and grain would suffer no instability…

title: 弘治二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之患武功著而國勢尊義聲揚而王靈振國家
之福寔不出此而文王之所以篤周祜者寧不
在兹哉一方倡亂四國靡寧王事多艱豈天下
之心哉故我文王之伐密也不過欲討彼有罪
使四方無鋒鏑之苦弔此無罪使萬姓有室家
之安戰鬭息而上下寧禍亂平而遐邇悅天下
之心夫豈外是而文王之所以對天下者寧不
在兹哉一伐密耳國祚以之而靈長民心以之
而悅服然亦因其可怒而怒之初豈有所畔援
歆羨哉此所以為文王之師也歟於虖豈獨伐
密哉有苗之格南巢之放牧野之誅其心一也
是何也盖行一不義殺一不辜而得天下不為
者千聖同一道也後世之師不出於憤則出於
貪不出於貪則出於驕流為窮黷無所不至是
又議興師者之所當知
春秋
齊人伐衞衞人及齊人戰衞人敗績〔莊公二十八年〕
===
晉荀林父帥師及楚子戰于邲
punctuated:
之患。武功著而國勢尊，義聲揚而王靈振，國家之福寔不出此，而文王之所以篤周祜者，寧不在兹哉？一方倡亂，四國靡寧，王事多艱，豈天下之心哉？故我文王之伐密也，不過欲討彼有罪，使四方無鋒鏑之苦；弔此無罪，使萬姓有室家之安。戰鬭息而上下寧，禍亂平而遐邇悅，天下之心夫豈外是，而文王之所以對天下者，寧不在兹哉？一伐密耳，國祚以之而靈長，民心以之而悅服，然亦因其可怒而怒之，初豈有所畔援歆羨哉？此所以為文王之師也歟！於虖！豈獨伐密哉？有苗之格，南巢之放，牧野之誅，其心一也。是何也？盖行一不義，殺一不辜，而得天下不為者，千聖同一道也。後世之師，不出於憤，則出於貪；不出於貪，則出於驕，流為窮黷，無所不至。是又議興師者之所當知。

春秋

齊人伐衞，衞人及齊人戰，衞人敗績。〔莊公二十八年〕

晉荀林父帥師及楚子戰于邲
translation_en:
…from the danger of instability. With military achievements manifest, the state's standing was exalted; with its reputation for righteousness spreading, royal authority was invigorated. The state's blessings lay precisely in this. Was this not how King Wen increased Zhou's blessings? When one region fomented disorder, the states on every side had no peace, and royal affairs were beset with difficulties—could this be what the people of the realm desired? Thus our King Wen's campaign against Mi sought only to punish the guilty, so that the people everywhere would be spared the suffering of blades and arrows, and to comfort the innocent, so that all the people might enjoy security in their homes. Fighting ceased, and high and low were at peace; calamity and disorder were quelled, and those far and near rejoiced. What else could the people of the realm desire? Was this not how King Wen answered their wishes? Through this single campaign against Mi, the dynasty's blessed tenure was prolonged, and the people's hearts submitted gladly. Yet his anger arose only because their conduct deserved anger: from the outset, how could he have been swayed by other aims or covetous desires? Surely this is what made it King Wen's army!

Ah! Was this true only of the campaign against Mi? The submission of the Youmiao, the banishment to Nanchao, and the punitive campaign at Muye all sprang from the same intent. Why was this? To refuse to commit a single unrighteous act or kill a single innocent person even to gain the realm—this is the one Way shared by all sages. The armies of later ages arose, if not from anger, then from greed; if not from greed, then from arrogance. They degenerated into exhausting and wanton warfare, stopping at nothing. This, too, is something those who deliberate on raising an army ought to understand.

Spring and Autumn Annals

The men of Qi attacked Wei. The men of Wei fought the men of Qi, and the men of Wei suffered a crushing defeat. 〔Twenty-eighth year of Duke Zhuang.〕

Xun Linfu of Jin led an army into battle against the Viscount of Chu at Bi…

title: 弘治二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
晋師敗績〔宣公十二年〕季孫行父臧孫許
叔孫僑如公孫嬰齊帥師會晉郤克
衛孫良夫曹公子首及齊侯戰于鞌
齊師敗績〔成公二年〕
洪世傅
同考試官訓導章批此題一木胡傳立說作者多
失㫖此篇剖析常變之例明白允宜錄出
考試官敎諭周批得聖人書法
考試官敎諭吳批合傳意
===
春秋紀兵既常例以立法復變例以示戒夫兵
有國之大事也春秋於內外之交兵得不致意
於將副主客之間哉何則衛黨子頹得罪於周
齊因錫命而伐衛楚莊竊伯舉兵爭鄭晉因救
鄭而戰邲衛之伐也主兵者齊宜以齊為主邲
之戰也六卿偕行宜將副並書春秋一則以衛
主戰一則獨書林父何耶凡伐者為客受伐者
為主例也今齊人奉命討罪衛人不能徵詞請
罪而憤然與之接戰則是衛人為志乎是戰豈
punctuated:
晋師敗績〔宣公十二年〕。季孫行父、臧孫許、叔孫僑如、公孫嬰齊帥師，會晉郤克、衛孫良夫、曹公子首，及齊侯戰于鞌，齊師敗績〔成公二年〕。
洪世傅。
同考試官訓導章批：此題一木胡傳立說，作者多失㫖。此篇剖析常變之例，明白允宜，錄出。
考試官敎諭周批：得聖人書法。
考試官敎諭吳批：合傳意。
春秋紀兵，既常例以立法，復變例以示戒。夫兵，有國之大事也。春秋於內外之交兵，得不致意於將副主客之間哉？何則？衛黨子頹，得罪於周，齊因錫命而伐衛；楚莊竊伯，舉兵爭鄭，晉因救鄭而戰邲。衛之伐也，主兵者齊，宜以齊為主；邲之戰也，六卿偕行，宜將副並書。春秋一則以衛主戰，一則獨書林父，何耶？凡伐者為客，受伐者為主，例也。今齊人奉命討罪，衛人不能徵詞請罪，而憤然與之接戰，則是衛人為志乎是戰，豈
translation_en:
…The army of Jin suffered a crushing defeat. 〔Twelfth year of Duke Xuan〕 Jisun Xingfu, Zangsun Xu, Shusun Qiaoru, and Gongsun Yingqi led an army and joined Xi Ke of Jin, Sun Liangfu of Wei, and Prince Shou of Cao in battle against the Marquis of Qi at An. The army of Qi suffered a crushing defeat. 〔Second year of Duke Cheng〕
Hong Shifu.
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Assistant Instructor: This topic bases its argument entirely on Hu’s Commentary [?], but writers mostly miss its purport. This essay analyzes the regular and exceptional conventions clearly and soundly. Selected for inclusion.
Comment by Examiner Zhou, Instructor: It grasps the Sage’s method of recording events.
Comment by Examiner Wu, Instructor: It accords with the meaning of the Commentary.
In recording military affairs, the Spring and Autumn Annals both establishes standards through regular conventions and conveys warnings through exceptional conventions. Warfare is a great affair of state. When recording hostilities between Lu and other states, or among other states, could the Annals fail to attend to the distinctions between commanders and deputies, and between defenders and attackers? Why is this so? Wei supported Zitui and thereby offended Zhou; Qi received a royal command and attacked Wei. King Zhuang of Chu usurped the position of hegemon and raised troops to contend for control of Zheng; Jin fought at Bi in order to rescue Zheng. In the attack on Wei, Qi directed the military action, so Qi ought to have been presented as the principal actor. In the battle of Bi, all six ministers went on the expedition, so both commanders and deputies ought to have been named. Yet in the first case the Annals presents Wei as initiating battle, and in the second it names Linfu alone. Why?
As a general convention, the attacking party is the guest and the party attacked is the host. Here, the men of Qi were carrying out a command to punish wrongdoing. The men of Wei failed to present an explanation [?] and ask forgiveness for their offense, but instead angrily engaged them in battle. Thus it was the men of Wei who were intent upon this battle. How could this…

title: 弘治二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
息爭之道乎將稱元帥畧其副屬詞之體也今
林父身為元帥不能禁副屬之違令顧乃知難
冒進棄其師而取敗豈專制之義乎故春秋於
伐衛以衛及齊于邲獨書林父非所謂常例以
立法者乎至若齊頃當國不能謹禮因房帷笑
客之故致四國伐齊之舉魯則季孫主將三國
則上卿舉兵以將副之例觀之宜畧諸帥而獨
書季孫以主客之例觀之宜釋諸國而以齊為
主春秋於此以四卿並列異乎于邲之書以四
===
國及齊異乎伐衛之文何耶盖爭忿小故謂之
憤兵今諸國大夫含憤積怒欲雪一笑之耻殘
民毒衆以快報復之私憤孰甚焉履霜堅氷漸
不可長今魯為季孫一怒掃境內興師雖無人
乎成公之側有不恤也然後政自季氏出矣專
莫甚焉故春秋於戰鞌以四國為主而列四卿
於會非所謂變例以示戒者乎吁受伐者為主
例也而又有伐者為主之詞將稱元帥例也而
又有將副並書之文聖人書法有常有變義各
punctuated: 息爭之道乎？將稱元帥，畧其副，屬詞之體也。今林父身為元帥，不能禁副屬之違令，顧乃知難冒進，棄其師而取敗，豈專制之義乎？故春秋於伐衛，以衛及齊；于邲，獨書林父，非所謂常例以立法者乎？至若齊頃當國，不能謹禮，因房帷笑客之故，致四國伐齊之舉。魯則季孫主將，三國則上卿舉兵。以將副之例觀之，宜畧諸帥而獨書季孫；以主客之例觀之，宜釋諸國而以齊為主。春秋於此，以四卿並列，異乎于邲之書；以四國及齊，異乎伐衛之文，何耶？盖爭忿小故，謂之憤兵。今諸國大夫含憤積怒，欲雪一笑之耻，殘民毒衆，以快報復之私，憤孰甚焉？履霜堅氷，漸不可長。今魯為季孫一怒，掃境內興師，雖無人乎成公之側，有不恤也。然後政自季氏出矣，專莫甚焉。故春秋於戰鞌，以四國為主，而列四卿於會，非所謂變例以示戒者乎？吁！受伐者為主，例也，而又有伐者為主之詞；將稱元帥，例也，而又有將副並書之文。聖人書法有常有變，義各
translation_en:
…is this the way to put an end to contention? To name the commander-in-chief while omitting his deputy is the proper form of wording. Now Linfu, although commander-in-chief, could not prevent his subordinate commanders from disobeying orders. Instead, knowing the difficulties, he rashly advanced, abandoned his army, and brought defeat upon himself. How could this accord with the principle of exercising sole command? Thus, in recording the attack on Wei, the Spring and Autumn Annals places Wei before Qi; at Bi, it names Linfu alone. Is this not what is meant by establishing rules through regular conventions?

As for Duke Qing of Qi, while ruling the state he failed to observe ritual propriety. Laughter directed at a guest from behind the curtains of the inner apartments brought about an expedition against Qi by four states. In Lu, Jisun was the principal commander, while in the other three states senior ministers led the troops. Judged by the convention governing commanders and deputies, the other commanders should have been omitted and Jisun alone named. Judged by the convention governing the defending and attacking parties, the other states should have been set aside and Qi made the principal party. Yet here the Spring and Autumn Annals lists all four ministers together, unlike its record of Bi; it places the four states before Qi, unlike its wording for the attack on Wei. Why?

Warfare arising from anger over a petty matter is called warfare of resentment. Now the grandees of these states harbored resentment and accumulated anger, wishing to wipe away the humiliation of a single laugh. They ravaged the people and afflicted the multitude to gratify their private desire for revenge. What resentment could be greater? Treading on frost foretells solid ice: such a tendency must not be allowed to grow. Now Lu, because of a single outburst of anger by Jisun, mobilized its entire territory and raised an army. Even if there was no one at Duke Cheng’s side, this showed disregard for him [?]. Thereafter government issued from the Ji lineage. No usurpation of authority could be greater. Thus, in recording the battle of An, the Spring and Autumn Annals makes the four states the principal party and lists the four ministers at the meeting. Is this not what is meant by departing from regular conventions to convey a warning?

Ah! It is the convention to make the party under attack the principal party, yet there is also wording that makes the attacking party principal. It is the convention to name the commander-in-chief, yet there are also passages naming both commander and deputy. The sage’s manner of recording events has both regular conventions and departures from them, each with its own meaning…

title: 弘治二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
君子所耻今魯不能謀國有道折衝禦侮吳兵
方至國猶可為遂有城下之盟東陽甫克患猶
未迫遽為下敵之舉失節辱國恬不為耻偷安
苟免自為得計向使魯能自强謀國如宋華元
以國斃而不從齊國佐合餘燼以借戰何至有
城下受盟之辱况吳輕而逺不久將歸乎故春
秋書伐我不言四鄙及與吳盟者欲見受盟之
實而深諱之也未幾我哀公十一年齊人以師
郕之故國書為伐魯之舉師自臨淄及清涉泗
===
春秋於此非有城下之盟可諱之辱亦書伐我
何哉誠以處己貴乎躬自厚而薄責於人彼自
反而縮君子所予今魯不思理曲在我而直在
彼開門延盜會吳伐齊師郕之兵方卷甲而歸
國書之報不旋踵而至構怨連禍惟其所召殘
民毒衆伊誰之咎向使魯能戒其輕動鑒傅說
甲冑起戎之言曾子出爾反爾之語何至有國
書見伐之慘况齊本甥舅世締其好乎故春秋
記斯師特書曰伐我欲省致師之由而躬自責
punctuated:
君子所耻。今魯不能謀國有道，折衝禦侮。吳兵方至，國猶可為，遂有城下之盟；東陽甫克，患猶未迫，遽為下敵之舉。失節辱國，恬不為耻；偷安苟免，自為得計。向使魯能自强，謀國如宋華元以國斃而不從、齊國佐合餘燼以借戰，何至有城下受盟之辱？况吳輕而逺，不久將歸乎？故《春秋》書「伐我」，不言四鄙及與吳盟者，欲見受盟之實而深諱之也。未幾，我哀公十一年，齊人以師郕之故，國書為伐魯之舉，師自臨淄及清，涉泗。
《春秋》於此，非有城下之盟可諱之辱，亦書「伐我」，何哉？誠以處己貴乎躬自厚而薄責於人，彼自反而縮，君子所予。今魯不思理曲在我而直在彼，開門延盜，會吳伐齊。師郕之兵方卷甲而歸，國書之報不旋踵而至。構怨連禍，惟其所召；殘民毒衆，伊誰之咎？向使魯能戒其輕動，鑒傅說「甲冑起戎」之言、曾子「出爾反爾」之語，何至有國書見伐之慘？况齊本甥舅，世締其好乎？故《春秋》記斯師，特書曰「伐我」，欲省致師之由而躬自責
translation_en:
…what a gentleman finds shameful. Now Lu could not devise sound plans for the state, repel aggression, and resist humiliation. When Wu’s troops first arrived, something could still have been done for the state, yet Lu entered into a covenant beneath its city walls. Dongyang had only just been taken, and the danger was not yet pressing, yet Lu hastily submitted to the enemy. It forfeited its integrity and humiliated the state, remaining untroubled by shame; it sought temporary ease and merely to escape disaster, considering this a sound strategy. Had Lu strengthened itself and planned for the state as Hua Yuan of Song did, preferring the state’s destruction to submission, or as Guo Zuo of Qi did, gathering the surviving remnants to risk another battle [?], how could it have suffered the humiliation of accepting a covenant beneath its walls? Moreover, Wu’s forces were impetuous and far from home, and would soon withdraw. Thus, when the Spring and Autumn Annals records “attacked us,” without mentioning any of the four border regions or the making of a covenant with Wu, its purpose is to reveal the fact that Lu accepted an imposed covenant while carefully veiling the disgrace. Not long afterward, in the eleventh year of our Duke Ai, because of the campaign against Cheng, Guo Shu of Qi undertook an attack on Lu. His army marched from Linzi to Qing and crossed the Si River.
Here there was no humiliation of a covenant beneath the city walls for the Spring and Autumn Annals to veil, yet it likewise records “attacked us.” Why? It is surely because, in conducting oneself, what matters is to demand much of oneself and blame others sparingly. Those who examine themselves and find themselves in the right earn a gentleman’s approval. Now Lu failed to consider that the wrong lay with us and the right with the other side. It opened its gates to invite in bandits, joining Wu in attacking Qi. The troops that had campaigned against Cheng had only just rolled up their armor and returned when Guo Shu’s retaliation arrived hard on their heels. Lu itself had invited these enmities and successive disasters. Whose fault was the devastation and suffering inflicted on the people? Had Lu guarded against rash action and taken warning from Fu Yue’s words, “Armor and helmets provoke warfare,” and Zengzi’s saying, “What goes out from you comes back to you,” how could it have suffered the calamity of Guo Shu’s attack? Moreover, Qi and Lu were related as maternal uncle and nephew, and had maintained friendly ties for generations. Thus, in recording this campaign, the Spring and Autumn Annals specifically writes “attacked us,” intending that Lu reflect on what had brought the army upon it and blame itself…

title: 弘治二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
也吁始因吳伐我而春秋為魯諱下敵之辱繼
因齊伐我而春秋欲魯省致師之由聖人拳拳
為魯之意一何至歟雖然周公伯禽之魯以秉
周禮號稱人望聖人嘗有志於用魯奈何昭定
哀之春秋有名無實削弱滋甚三卿專政鄰國
交伐外有患而莫支内有變而不悟聖人望魯
之意至是絕矣諸侯欲於魯觀禮得乎噫此聖
人所以憂此春秋所以作
禮記
===
故聖人參於天地並於鬼神以治政也處
其所存禮之序也玩其所樂民之治
也故天生時而地生財人其父生而
師教之四者君以正用之故君者立
於無過之地也
洗睿
同考試官教諭朱批禮運一題本正大作者往往忽
之多分截不明此篇融會傳註組織成文發明聖
人治政之要無餘蘊矣宜為本房之冠
punctuated:
也。吁！始因吳伐我，而春秋為魯諱下敵之辱；繼因齊伐我，而春秋欲魯省致師之由。聖人拳拳為魯之意，一何至歟！雖然，周公伯禽之魯，以秉周禮號稱人望，聖人嘗有志於用魯。奈何昭、定、哀之春秋，有名無實，削弱滋甚，三卿專政，鄰國交伐，外有患而莫支，内有變而不悟。聖人望魯之意，至是絕矣。諸侯欲於魯觀禮，得乎？噫！此聖人所以憂，此春秋所以作。
禮記
故聖人參於天地，並於鬼神，以治政也。處其所存，禮之序也；玩其所樂，民之治也。故天生時，而地生財，人其父生而師教之。四者，君以正用之。故君者，立於無過之地也。
洗睿
同考試官教諭朱批：禮運一題，本正大，作者往往忽之，多分截不明。此篇融會傳註，組織成文，發明聖人治政之要，無餘蘊矣。宜為本房之冠。
translation_en:
…indeed. Ah! First, when Wu attacked us, the Spring and Autumn Annals concealed on Lu’s behalf the humiliation of submitting to an enemy; later, when Qi attacked us, the Spring and Autumn Annals wished Lu to examine why it had brought an invading army upon itself. How profound was the Sage’s devoted concern for Lu! Nevertheless, Lu, the state of the Duke of Zhou and Bo Qin, was renowned for upholding Zhou ritual and commanded people’s esteem. The Sage once aspired to put his principles into practice in Lu. Yet during the reigns of Dukes Zhao, Ding, and Ai, Lu possessed the name without the substance and grew increasingly weak. The three chief ministers monopolized government, and neighboring states attacked it in succession. It could not withstand troubles from outside and failed to awaken to upheavals within. At this point, the Sage’s hopes for Lu were exhausted. Could the regional lords still expect to observe proper ritual in Lu? Alas! This was what troubled the Sage; this was why the Spring and Autumn Annals was written.
Record of Rites
“Thus the sage forms a triad with Heaven and Earth and stands alongside the ghosts and spirits in conducting government. Taking his place where he belongs constitutes the ordering of ritual; attending to what he delights in constitutes the good governance of the people. Thus Heaven produces the seasons and Earth produces resources; a person’s father begets him and his teacher instructs him. The ruler employs these four correctly. Thus the ruler stands in a position free from error.”
Xian Rui
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhu, Instructor: “This topic from ‘The Operations of Ritual’ (Li yun) is fundamentally upright and grand, yet writers frequently overlook this. Most divide it into separate portions without making its meaning clear. This essay integrates the commentaries and annotations, weaving them into a coherent composition. It elucidates the essentials of the sage’s conduct of government, leaving no underlying meaning unexplored. It deserves first place among the essays in this examining room.”

title: 弘治二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭周批詞能說理尤勝他作
考試官教諭吳批通篇措詞簡當諸卷中盖
無出其右者
論聖人合造化以治政而政所由治必推言治
政在乎正身也盖参並造化以治政惟聖人而
後能也然則治政之要舍君身之正而立於無
過之地何以哉記者論聖人庸禮之政而及此
且君者政之所自出政者君之所由安是以聖
人之和國也天地至大而難量則有以参賛其
===
道而為三焉鬼神至幽而難測則有以擬並其
事而無間焉所以参之並之者無他凡以治政
而已矣政莫大於禮之序聖人處天地鬼神之
所存于以法其高下散殊之理此禮之所以序
也政莫大於民之治聖人玩天地鬼神之所樂
于以法其周流同化之機此民之所以治也然
聖人果何法此以治政耶誠以時生於天貨産
於地天時地利莫非政之所關人生於父德成
於師父生師教罔非政之攸寓四者之政治之
punctuated:
考試官教諭周批：詞能說理，尤勝他作。
考試官教諭吳批：通篇措詞簡當，諸卷中盖無出其右者。
論聖人合造化以治政，而政所由治，必推言治政在乎正身也。盖参並造化以治政，惟聖人而後能也。然則治政之要，舍君身之正而立於無過之地，何以哉？記者論聖人庸禮之政而及此。且君者，政之所自出；政者，君之所由安。是以聖人之和國也，天地至大而難量，則有以参賛其道而為三焉；鬼神至幽而難測，則有以擬並其事而無間焉。所以参之並之者無他，凡以治政而已矣。政莫大於禮之序，聖人處天地鬼神之所存，于以法其高下散殊之理，此禮之所以序也。政莫大於民之治，聖人玩天地鬼神之所樂，于以法其周流同化之機，此民之所以治也。然聖人果何法此以治政耶？誠以時生於天，貨産於地，天時地利莫非政之所關；人生於父，德成於師，父生師教罔非政之攸寓。四者之政，治之
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Zhou, Instructor: The wording explains the principles effectively and is especially superior to other compositions.

Comment by Examiner Wu, Instructor: The wording throughout is concise and apt. Among all the papers, there is probably none that surpasses it.

In discussing how the sage unites with the processes of creation and transformation to govern, one must trace the source of orderly government to the rectification of the ruler’s own person. Only a sage can participate in and stand alongside creation and transformation in governing. What, then, could be the essential means of governing, apart from the ruler’s rectifying himself and establishing himself in a position free from error? The author of the Record reaches this point in discussing the sage’s government through ritual. Moreover, the ruler is the source from which government issues, and government is the means by which the ruler secures his peace. Thus, when the sage brings harmony to the state, although Heaven and Earth are supremely vast and difficult to fathom, he can assist their Way and form a triad with them; although ghosts and spirits are supremely hidden and difficult to discern, he can emulate and match their operations without any discrepancy. His purpose in participating alongside them is nothing other than to govern.

In government, nothing is greater than the proper ordering of ritual. The sage places himself within that which Heaven, Earth, ghosts, and spirits preserve, thereby taking as his model their principle of higher and lower ranks and manifold distinctions. This is how ritual is ordered. In government, nothing is greater than bringing order to the people. The sage contemplates what Heaven, Earth, ghosts, and spirits delight in, thereby taking as his model the workings of their all-pervading circulation and shared transformation. This is how the people are brought to order.

Yet how, precisely, does the sage model himself on these things in governing? It is because the seasons arise from Heaven and material goods are produced by Earth: the seasons of Heaven and the advantages of Earth are all concerns of government. A person is begotten by his father, and his virtue is perfected by his teacher: the father’s begetting and the teacher’s instruction are both spheres in which government resides. As for governance in these four matters, to govern them …

title: 弘治二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
不有其要哉亦曰君以正用之而已于焉正身
脩德其於天時也地利也順之因之無所違體
元居正其於父生也師教也左之右之無所拂
曰順之曰因之則治道以張其要不在君身之
正而立於無過之地乎曰左之曰右之則治道
以得其要不在君德之脩而處於至正之域乎
噫治政在乎正身如此則聖人之所以參天地
而並鬼神者其以是哉大抵人君治政能參三
才之功固自正身中來也求之古人孰可以當
===
之觀夫欽明文思允恭克讓堯之身正何如也
敬天授時之政一行而黎民有於變之風濬哲
文明温恭允塞舜之身正何若也封山濬川之
政一舉而四方有風動之休噫此堯舜所以為
萬世君人之法也歟
養其身以有為也
黃著
同考試官教諭朱 批 題本上文立說似易而實難
於作者此篇文理通暢說出儒者備豫之行深合
punctuated:
不有其要哉？亦曰君以正用之而已。于焉正身脩德，其於天時也、地利也，順之因之，無所違；體元居正，其於父生也、師教也，左之右之，無所拂。曰順之，曰因之，則治道以張，其要不在君身之正，而立於無過之地乎？曰左之，曰右之，則治道以得，其要不在君德之脩，而處於至正之域乎？噫！治政在乎正身如此，則聖人之所以參天地而並鬼神者，其以是哉！大抵人君治政，能參三才之功，固自正身中來也。求之古人，孰可以當之？觀夫欽明文思，允恭克讓，堯之身正何如也！敬天授時之政一行，而黎民有於變之風。濬哲文明，温恭允塞，舜之身正何若也！封山濬川之政一舉，而四方有風動之休。噫！此堯舜所以為萬世君人之法也歟！

養其身以有為也。
黃著

同考試官教諭朱批：題本上文立說，似易而實難於作者。此篇文理通暢，說出儒者備豫之行，深合
translation_en:
…is there not an essential principle? It is simply that the ruler employs them with rectitude. Thus, by rectifying his person and cultivating his virtue, he follows Heaven’s seasons and makes use of the advantages of the earth, opposing neither. By embodying the primal principle and abiding in rectitude, he supports and assists the father’s giving of life and the teacher’s instruction, obstructing neither. Through following and making use of them, the Way of government is extended. Does its essential principle not lie in the ruler’s personal rectitude, whereby he stands free of error? Through supporting and assisting them, the Way of government is attained. Does its essential principle not lie in the cultivation of the ruler’s virtue, whereby he abides in perfect rectitude? Ah! Since governing depends in this way upon rectifying one’s person, must this not be how the sage forms a triad with Heaven and Earth and stands alongside the spirits? In general, a ruler’s ability, in governing, to participate in the achievements of the Three Powers—Heaven, Earth, and humanity—certainly proceeds from rectifying his person. Among the ancients, who could exemplify this?

Consider Yao: reverent, discerning, accomplished, and thoughtful, truly respectful and capable of yielding. How upright was his person! Once he put into practice government that revered Heaven and provided the people with the proper seasonal calendar, the common people underwent a transformation. Profoundly wise, accomplished and discerning, gentle and respectful, sincere and trustworthy—how upright was Shun’s person! Once he undertook measures to delimit the mountains and dredge the rivers, the four quarters enjoyed the blessing of responding as if moved by the wind. Ah! Is this not why Yao and Shun serve as models for rulers throughout all ages?

“He cultivates his person so that he may accomplish something.”
By Huang Zhu 黃著.

title: 弘治二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
本旨是宜錄出
考試官教諭周批文不蹈襲能發明聖人告哀
公之意
考試官教諭吳批本傳註立說而辭氣整潔
可嘉
儒者豫養乎身正欲有應於世盖事豫則立也
苟不能豫養是身以應世又豈儒者備豫之行
哉聖人告哀公之意如此且儒者講學於閒燕
從容乎席上以為吾之一身關天下之大不有
===
以豫養之則身不立而德不充矣將何以有為
哉由是居處齋難而坐起恭敬言必先信而行
必中正則敬有以養其身矣於道途也不爭險
易之利於冬夏也不爭陰陽之和則恕有以養
其身矣夫如是則忿懲慾窒身立德充不惟可
以當天下之變而不避而又可以任天下之重
而不辭將見生民命脉待我而培養國家元氣
待我而扶持以之為股肱為心膂則致吾君為
堯舜之君所謂為上為德者是已何嘗辭其任
punctuated:
本旨，是宜錄出。
考試官教諭周批：文不蹈襲，能發明聖人告哀公之意。
考試官教諭吳批：本傳註立說，而辭氣整潔，可嘉。
儒者豫養乎身，正欲有應於世，盖事豫則立也。苟不能豫養是身以應世，又豈儒者備豫之行哉？聖人告哀公之意如此。且儒者講學於閒燕，從容乎席上，以為吾之一身關天下之大，不有以豫養之，則身不立而德不充矣，將何以有為哉？由是居處齋難，而坐起恭敬，言必先信，而行必中正，則敬有以養其身矣。於道途也，不爭險易之利；於冬夏也，不爭陰陽之和，則恕有以養其身矣。夫如是，則忿懲慾窒，身立德充，不惟可以當天下之變而不避，而又可以任天下之重而不辭。將見生民命脉待我而培養，國家元氣待我而扶持。以之為股肱，為心膂，則致吾君為堯舜之君，所謂為上為德者是已。何嘗辭其任
translation_en:
…the original purport; it therefore deserves to be included.

Examiner Zhou, an Instructor, comments: The essay does not imitate earlier writing and brings out the meaning of the sage’s words to Duke Ai.

Examiner Wu, an Instructor, comments: Its argument rests on the commentaries and annotations, and its language and tone are orderly and clean. It merits praise.

The Confucian scholar cultivates himself in advance precisely so that he may respond to the needs of the world, for undertakings succeed when prepared beforehand. If he cannot cultivate himself beforehand to respond to the world, how could this constitute the Confucian scholar’s practice of preparedness? Such was the meaning of the sage’s words to Duke Ai. Moreover, when the Confucian scholar discusses learning in quiet leisure, sitting at ease upon his mat, he reflects: “My own person bears upon the great affairs of all under Heaven. Unless I cultivate myself beforehand, my character will not be established and my virtue will not be full. How, then, could I accomplish anything?” Thus, he is solemn and circumspect in his daily conduct, and respectful when sitting or rising. In speech he puts trustworthiness first, and in action he invariably accords with uprightness and the mean. Through reverence, then, he cultivates himself. On the roads, he does not contend for the advantage of an easy rather than a difficult route; in winter and summer, he does not contend for the comfort of shade or sunshine. Through consideration for others, then, he cultivates himself.

Acting thus, he restrains anger and checks desires; his character is established and his virtue full. Not only can he confront upheavals under Heaven without evading them, but he can also shoulder the weighty responsibilities of the world without declining them. We shall then see the people’s lifeblood awaiting his nurture, and the state’s vital energies awaiting his support. Serving as his ruler’s arms and legs, heart and backbone, he brings his ruler to become a ruler like Yao or Shun. This is what is meant by acting for virtue when serving those above. When has he ever declined the responsibilities he bears…

title: 弘治二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之重哉以之作舟楫作霖雨則澤吾民為堯舜
之民所謂為下為民者是已何嘗辭其責之重
哉噫儒者養身有為如此其備豫之行至矣聖
人舉之以告哀公得無意乎抑考儒行一篇昔
哀公覘孔子被服儒雅威儀進趨與俗不同怪
而問之孔子既以不知儒服告之及問儒行而
又悉數之者無非望其崇重吾儒也厥後哀公
言加信行加義不敢以儒為戲容或有以感動
之歟惜乎終不能用孔子此魯之所以終於不
===
振而深可為之太息
第貳場
論
帝王臨御天下
區元廣
同考試官學正章 批此論歷數古今華夷之事殆
盡且以我
聖祖為二帝三王以來一人而已其知言哉讀之真令萬世中國一快然也得士如斯亦可以報
上矣
punctuated:
之重哉？以之作舟楫、作霖雨，則澤吾民為堯舜之民，所謂為下為民者是已，何嘗辭其責之重哉？噫！儒者養身有為如此，其備豫之行至矣。聖人舉之以告哀公，得無意乎？抑考《儒行》一篇，昔哀公覘孔子被服儒雅，威儀進趨與俗不同，怪而問之。孔子既以不知儒服告之，及問儒行，而又悉數之者，無非望其崇重吾儒也。厥後哀公言加信，行加義，不敢以儒為戲，容或有以感動之歟？惜乎終不能用孔子，此魯之所以終於不振，而深可為之太息。

第貳場

論

帝王臨御天下

區元廣

同考試官學正章批：此論歷數古今華夷之事殆盡，且以我聖祖為二帝三王以來一人而已，其知言哉！讀之真令萬世中國一快然也。得士如斯，亦可以報上矣。
translation_en:
…the weight of his charge? By serving as boat and oars, and as timely rain, he brings blessings to our people, making them like the people of Yao and Shun. This is what is meant by acting for those below, for the people. When has he ever shirked the weight of his responsibility? Ah! The Confucian scholar cultivates himself for purposes such as these: his practice of preparedness is consummate. Could the Sage have had no purpose in setting this before Duke Ai? Consider, moreover, the chapter “The Conduct of the Confucian Scholar.” Formerly, Duke Ai observed that Confucius’s clothing was refined and scholarly, and that his dignified bearing and movements differed from ordinary custom. Puzzled, he questioned him. Confucius first told him that he did not know what constituted a scholar’s dress; then, when asked about a scholar’s conduct, he enumerated it fully. His sole hope was that the duke would honor and esteem our scholars. Thereafter, Duke Ai became more trustworthy in speech and more righteous in conduct, and dared not make sport of scholars. Might something in these words have moved him? Alas, in the end he could not employ Confucius. This is why Lu ultimately failed to recover its strength—a matter deeply deserving of lamentation.

Second Session

Discourse

“Emperors and Kings Preside over All under Heaven”

Ou Yuanguang

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, School Instructor: This discourse recounts almost exhaustively the affairs of Chinese and non-Chinese peoples, past and present. Moreover, it regards our sagely founder as the one peerless figure since the Two Emperors and Three Kings. How discerning its words are! Reading it truly brings great satisfaction to China for all ages. By obtaining a scholar such as this, we too can repay His Majesty.

title: 弘治二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭周批論有抑揚可取
考試官教諭吳批有證據起伏真傑作也
以天下之大而主之一人天之意其有在
哉蓋天地不可一日無人紀無人紀是無
人也無人是無天地也世至無天地亦極
矣天豈終恝然哉於是必生聖人而以是
付之焉何以言之蓋極天地之所覆載極
日月之所照臨此天下之大形勢也內則
中國外則夷狄此天下之大界限也夷狄
===
不可為中國中國不可為夷狄此天下之
大名分也夷狄犯中國則誅之中國而夷
狄則夷狄之此天下之大防閑也中國有
三綱夷狄無三綱中國有五常夷狄無五
常中國有禮義夷狄無禮義中國有教化
夷狄無教化中國有封建夷狄無有也中
國有井田夷狄無有也禮樂刑政中國有
而夷狄無也紀綱法度中國有而夷狄無
也此則天下之大區別也天下有帝王則
punctuated:
考試官教諭周批：論有抑揚，可取。
考試官教諭吳批：有證據起伏，真傑作也。
以天下之大而主之一人，天之意其有在哉！蓋天地不可一日無人紀，無人紀是無人也，無人是無天地也。世至無天地，亦極矣，天豈終恝然哉？於是必生聖人而以是付之焉。何以言之？蓋極天地之所覆載，極日月之所照臨，此天下之大形勢也。內則中國，外則夷狄，此天下之大界限也。夷狄不可為中國，中國不可為夷狄，此天下之大名分也。夷狄犯中國則誅之，中國而夷狄則夷狄之，此天下之大防閑也。中國有三綱，夷狄無三綱；中國有五常，夷狄無五常；中國有禮義，夷狄無禮義；中國有教化，夷狄無教化；中國有封建，夷狄無有也；中國有井田，夷狄無有也；禮樂刑政，中國有而夷狄無也；紀綱法度，中國有而夷狄無也。此則天下之大區別也。天下有帝王，則
translation_en:
Examiner Zhou, Instructor, comments: “The discourse has effective contrasts of emphasis and restraint and merits acceptance.”
Examiner Wu, Instructor, comments: “It offers supporting evidence and has rises and falls in its composition—a true masterpiece.”
For all the vastness of all under Heaven, a single person is made its ruler: surely Heaven has a purpose in this! Heaven and Earth cannot go a single day without the ordering principles of human relationships. Without these principles, there would be no humanity; without humanity, there would be no Heaven and Earth. For the world to reach the point of having neither Heaven nor Earth would be the ultimate extremity. Could Heaven remain indifferent forever? Thus it must bring forth a sage and entrust him with all this. How can this be explained? Extending to the utmost bounds of what Heaven covers and Earth bears, and of what the sun and moon illuminate: this is the great configuration of all under Heaven. Within lies the Central Realm; outside lie the barbarians: this is the great boundary of all under Heaven. Barbarians may not become the Central Realm, and the Central Realm may not become barbarian: this is the great distinction of status in all under Heaven. If barbarians invade the Central Realm, they are to be punished; if those of the Central Realm act as barbarians, they are to be treated as barbarians: these are the great safeguards of all under Heaven. The Central Realm has the Three Bonds; the barbarians have no Three Bonds. The Central Realm has the Five Constant Virtues; the barbarians have no Five Constant Virtues. The Central Realm has ritual propriety and righteousness; the barbarians have neither. The Central Realm has moral instruction and transformation; the barbarians have neither. The Central Realm has the system of enfeoffment; the barbarians do not. The Central Realm has the well-field system; the barbarians do not. Ritual, music, punishments, and government exist in the Central Realm but not among the barbarians. Principles of order, laws, and institutions exist in the Central Realm but not among the barbarians. These are the great distinctions within all under Heaven. When all under Heaven has emperors and kings, then…

title: 弘治二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
其大形勢自尊天下有帝王則其大界限
自明天下有帝王則其大名分自正天下
有帝王則其大防閑自嚴天下之三綱必
自帝王而始敘天下之五常必自帝王而
始明天下之禮義非帝王無自而惇天下
之教化非帝王無自而彰天下之封建非
帝王不能行天下之井田非帝王不能定
天下之禮樂刑政必帝王而后四達天下
之紀綱法度必帝王而后一統此天下之
===
大區別必帝王而后大明白也是知天下
不可一日不繫屬於帝王而帝王亦不可
一日不維持乎天下也昔者舜御中國之
天下矣而蠻夷服昔者禹御中國之天下
矣而有苗格中國有湯而氐羌来享中國
有大王而串夷載路有周之盛時中國天
下有人而獫狁于夷有周之中興中國天
下有人而蠻荊来威是時中國為中國夷
狄為夷狄非惟中國治夷狄亦治非惟中
punctuated:
其大形勢自尊。天下有帝王，則其大界限自明；天下有帝王，則其大名分自正；天下有帝王，則其大防閑自嚴。天下之三綱，必自帝王而始敘；天下之五常，必自帝王而始明。天下之禮義，非帝王無自而惇；天下之教化，非帝王無自而彰。天下之封建，非帝王不能行；天下之井田，非帝王不能定。天下之禮樂刑政，必帝王而后四達；天下之紀綱法度，必帝王而后一統。此天下之大區別，必帝王而后大明白也。是知天下不可一日不繫屬於帝王，而帝王亦不可一日不維持乎天下也。
昔者舜御中國之天下矣，而蠻夷服；昔者禹御中國之天下矣，而有苗格。中國有湯，而氐羌来享；中國有大王，而串夷載路。有周之盛時，中國天下有人，而獫狁于夷；有周之中興，中國天下有人，而蠻荊来威。是時中國為中國，夷狄為夷狄，非惟中國治，夷狄亦治；非惟中
translation_en:
…its commanding position is naturally exalted. When All-under-Heaven has an emperor or king, its great boundaries naturally become clear; when it has an emperor or king, its fundamental distinctions of status naturally become correct; when it has an emperor or king, its great safeguards naturally become strict. The ordering of the Three Bonds throughout All-under-Heaven must begin with the emperor or king; the clarification of the Five Constant Virtues must begin with him. Without an emperor or king, ritual propriety and righteousness have no means of being cultivated, and moral instruction has no means of being made manifest. Only an emperor or king can implement the system of enfeoffment and establish the well-field system. Only with an emperor or king can rites, music, punishments, and government reach the four quarters, and can the governing principles, laws, and institutions be unified. These great distinctions within All-under-Heaven can become fully clear only with an emperor or king. Thus we know that All-under-Heaven cannot go a single day without being bound to an emperor or king, and that the emperor or king likewise cannot go a single day without sustaining All-under-Heaven.
In former times, Shun ruled over the realm of the Central States, and the Man and Yi submitted; Yu ruled over the realm of the Central States, and the Youmiao came into submission. When the Central States had Tang, the Di and Qiang came to present offerings; when the Central States had King Tai, the Chuan Yi were driven away [?]. At the height of the Zhou dynasty, the Central States and All-under-Heaven had a worthy ruler, and the Xianyun were pacified; during the Zhou restoration, the Central States and All-under-Heaven had a worthy ruler, and the Man of Jing came in submission to his might. At that time, the Central States fulfilled their role as the Central States, and the Yi and Di theirs as the Yi and Di. Not only were the Central States well governed, but the Yi and Di were also well governed; not only were the Central States…

title: 弘治二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
國安夷狄亦安自是以後不能無言焉以
秦皇之疆而終不敢窺西河以漢高之興
而幾不能脫平城狼居胥之封僅足以雪
七日之困辱呼韓邪之朝不足以償四海
之虛耗烏孫守禮西域佩印雖可為中國
之榮觀無益於中國之大本是時中國猶
自為中國夷狄猶自為夷狄終可言也至
如晉陽之旅資威於突厥靈武之師借勢
於回紇故中原之禍亂與唐世相始終是
===
時中國不善為中國夷狄不安為夷狄然
又可言也若夫澶淵之役猶貽後悔靖康
之讐不共戴天然猶未也至於南北之勢
已成而錢塘之潮不來矣閩廣之舟日南
而崖門之旗遂仆焉於乎天地之氣魄至
是索然沮喪日月之光華至是奄然晦蝕
中國之土地至是盡為朔漠中國之人民
至是盡為犬羊中國之冠弁至是盡為辮
髮中國之衣裳至是盡為左衽自古帝王
punctuated: 國安，夷狄亦安。自是以後，不能無言焉。以秦皇之疆，而終不敢窺西河；以漢高之興，而幾不能脫平城。狼居胥之封，僅足以雪七日之困辱；呼韓邪之朝，不足以償四海之虛耗。烏孫守禮，西域佩印，雖可為中國之榮觀，無益於中國之大本。是時中國猶自為中國，夷狄猶自為夷狄，終可言也。至如晉陽之旅，資威於突厥；靈武之師，借勢於回紇。故中原之禍亂，與唐世相始終。是時中國不善為中國，夷狄不安為夷狄，然又可言也。若夫澶淵之役，猶貽後悔；靖康之讐，不共戴天。然猶未也。至於南北之勢已成，而錢塘之潮不來矣；閩廣之舟日南，而崖門之旗遂仆焉。於乎！天地之氣魄至是索然沮喪，日月之光華至是奄然晦蝕，中國之土地至是盡為朔漠，中國之人民至是盡為犬羊，中國之冠弁至是盡為辮髮，中國之衣裳至是盡為左衽。自古帝王
translation_en:
…China was at peace, and the barbarians too were at peace. After this, however, matters cannot pass without comment. Despite the might of the Qin emperor, he ultimately dared not cast his eyes upon Xihe [?]; despite the rise of Gaozu of Han, he almost failed to escape from Pingcheng. The sacrifice at Mount Langjuxu barely sufficed to wipe away the humiliation of the seven-day siege; Huhanye’s appearance at court did not suffice to compensate for the exhaustion of resources throughout the realm. Wusun observed ritual propriety, and the Western Regions bore seals of office: although these might make a splendid spectacle for China, they brought no benefit to its fundamental foundations. At this time, China was still China, and the barbarians were still barbarians; there was, after all, still something to be said for this.

As for the army raised at Jinyang, it drew its might from the Tujue; the forces at Lingwu borrowed their strength from the Huihe. Thus calamity and disorder in the Central Plain accompanied the Tang dynasty from beginning to end. At this time, China did not properly conduct itself as China, and the barbarians were not content to remain barbarians. Yet even here there was still something to be said.

The campaign at Chanyuan left regrets for later generations; the enmity arising from Jingkang was such that the foes could not live beneath the same heaven. Yet this was not the end. Once the division between north and south had taken shape, the tide at Qiantang ceased to come. The ships of Min and Guang sailed farther south each day, and at last the banners at Yamen fell. Alas! At this point the vital spirit of Heaven and Earth was utterly dispirited; the radiance of sun and moon was suddenly darkened and eclipsed. All the lands of China became the northern desert; all the people of China became dogs and sheep. China’s ceremonial caps were all replaced by braided hair; China’s robes all became garments fastened on the left. The emperors and kings since antiquity …

title: 弘治二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
臨御天下之道至是蕩然無餘矣雲擾於
五胡何足言哉瓜分於五季何足言哉此
天下之大變自開闢以來未見也此天下
之大耻自開闢以來未聞也此天下之大
憤自開闢以來未有也是中國不中國夷
狄非夷狄矣十世之間九十年之內父不
父子不子夫不夫婦不婦而又重之以大
德不君泰定不臣天曆不弟腥氣熏天汚
流漲地人紀至是盡矣尚何言哉然地終
===
不可以為天夜終不可以為晝冬寒之極
必有陽春激湍之下必有深潭悠悠蒼天
能無意乎於是
淮甸之間
真主出焉拯一世於腥羶之中脫萬民於穢濁
之地天地已傾而復正日月已晦而復明
六合矇矇而復清四海棼棼而復理天下
之大形勢復尊天下之大界限復明天下
之大名分復正天下之大防閑復嚴天下
punctuated: 臨御天下之道，至是蕩然無餘矣。雲擾於五胡，何足言哉！瓜分於五季，何足言哉！此天下之大變，自開闢以來未見也；此天下之大耻，自開闢以來未聞也；此天下之大憤，自開闢以來未有也。是中國不中國，夷狄非夷狄矣。十世之間，九十年之內，父不父，子不子，夫不夫，婦不婦，而又重之以大德不君、泰定不臣、天曆不弟。腥氣熏天，汚流漲地，人紀至是盡矣，尚何言哉！然地終不可以為天，夜終不可以為晝。冬寒之極，必有陽春；激湍之下，必有深潭。悠悠蒼天，能無意乎？於是淮甸之間，真主出焉，拯一世於腥羶之中，脫萬民於穢濁之地。天地已傾而復正，日月已晦而復明，六合矇矇而復清，四海棼棼而復理。天下之大形勢復尊，天下之大界限復明，天下之大名分復正，天下之大防閑復嚴，天下
translation_en:
…the way of ruling All under Heaven had by this time been utterly swept away. What comparison could there be with the turmoil of the Five Hu? What comparison could there be with the partition of the realm during the Five Dynasties? This was a cataclysm for All under Heaven unseen since the beginning of creation; a humiliation unheard of since the beginning of creation; an outrage without precedent since the beginning of creation. China was no longer China, and the barbarians were no longer barbarians. Over ten generations, within ninety years, fathers failed to act as fathers, sons as sons, husbands as husbands, and wives as wives. Added to this were the failures of the Dade emperor to act as a ruler, the Taiding emperor to act as a subject, and the Tianli emperor to act as a younger brother. A rank stench rose to Heaven, and foul currents flooded the earth. The bonds of human relationships were now utterly exhausted. What more could be said?

Yet earth can never become Heaven, nor night become day. At the utmost extreme of winter’s cold, a warm spring must follow; beneath rushing rapids, there must be a deep pool. Could vast, blue Heaven have no purpose? Then, in the lands of the Huai, the true sovereign arose. He rescued an entire age from the rank and fetid midst and delivered the myriad people from a land of filth and pollution. Heaven and earth, already overturned, were set upright again; the sun and moon, already darkened, shone brightly again. The six directions, shrouded in obscurity, became clear again; the Four Seas, tangled in disorder, were brought to order again. The great configuration of power throughout All under Heaven regained its exalted standing; its great boundaries became clear again; its great distinctions of status were rectified again; its great safeguards became strict again; All under Heaven’s…

title: 弘治二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之大區別復大明白矣豈特可為趙氏一
大快實可為中國一大快也豈特可為一
世中國一大快實可為萬世中國一大快
也蓋自二帝三王以来一人而已豈區區
漢唐宋之足言哉此則我
太祖高皇帝之所以臨御天下也是皆
天之所為也臣嘗莊誦
北伐之檄而有以知其然矣其曰人君者斯
民之宗主朝廷者天下之根本禮義者御
===
世之大防是三言者舜之帝於虞禹之王
於夏湯之王於商大王文武宣王之君於
周我
聖祖之帝於我朝其本在是矣所謂萬古一心
千聖一道也臣故曰自二帝三王以来一
人而已
表
擬
車駕幸國子監祭酒率諸生謝表
punctuated:
之大區別復大明白矣。豈特可為趙氏一大快，實可為中國一大快也；豈特可為一世中國一大快，實可為萬世中國一大快也。蓋自二帝三王以来，一人而已，豈區區漢唐宋之足言哉！此則我太祖高皇帝之所以臨御天下也，是皆天之所為也。臣嘗莊誦北伐之檄，而有以知其然矣。其曰：「人君者，斯民之宗主；朝廷者，天下之根本；禮義者，御世之大防。」是三言者，舜之帝於虞，禹之王於夏，湯之王於商，大王文武宣王之君於周，我聖祖之帝於我朝，其本在是矣。所謂萬古一心，千聖一道也。臣故曰：自二帝三王以来，一人而已。

表

擬車駕幸國子監祭酒率諸生謝表
translation_en:
…the great distinctions under Heaven were once again made perfectly clear. This was not merely a great cause for rejoicing for the Zhao house, but truly a great cause for rejoicing for China; not merely for China in one age, but truly for China through all ages. Since the Two Emperors and Three Kings, there has been only this one man. How could the mere Han, Tang, and Song merit mention beside him? Such was the basis upon which our Emperor Taizu Gao came to rule all under Heaven. All this was Heaven’s doing.

Your servant has reverently recited the Proclamation for the Northern Expedition and thereby come to understand that this is so. It says: “The ruler is the sovereign lord of this people; the imperial court is the foundation of all under Heaven; ritual propriety and righteousness are the great safeguards for governing the world.” These three statements contain the foundation upon which Shun ruled as emperor in Yu, Yu as king in Xia, Tang as king in Shang, Kings Tai, Wen, Wu, and Xuan as rulers in Zhou, and our Sagely Progenitor as emperor of our dynasty. This is what is meant by “one mind throughout all ages, one Way shared by a thousand sages.” Thus your servant says: since the Two Emperors and Three Kings, there has been only this one man.

title: 弘治二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
道皆入大學允惟賢士之關於樂辟雍寔
乃名教之地墻高數仞風動四方盖天下
必有達尊而
盛德未甞自聖禮增釋菜意已默通於先師
幄次講堂心惟冀聞乎大道六經具在萬姓
環觀
作之君作之師於今為盛不如堯不如舜豈敢
以陳雖率舊章寔為盛節尊禮師傅事邁
漢皇大召名儒迹高唐帝堂堂乎示吾道
===
以指歸勃勃焉大斯文之氣魄
恩均六舘荷雨露以霑濡光被百僚慶風雲
之際會于今始見曠古希聞〔臣某〕等幸列
學官叨趨
輦路有慚待問空空然無地可逃莫罄名言
蕩蕩乎惟天為大涓埃何在海嶽奚裨伏
願
日就月將冀
聖學自今以始河清海晏祝
punctuated: 道。皆入大學，允惟賢士之關；於樂辟雍，寔乃名教之地。墻高數仞，風動四方。盖天下必有達尊，而盛德未甞自聖。禮增釋菜，意已默通於先師；幄次講堂，心惟冀聞乎大道。六經具在，萬姓環觀。作之君，作之師，於今為盛；不如堯，不如舜，豈敢以陳？雖率舊章，寔為盛節。尊禮師傅，事邁漢皇；大召名儒，迹高唐帝。堂堂乎示吾道以指歸，勃勃焉大斯文之氣魄。恩均六舘，荷雨露以霑濡；光被百僚，慶風雲之際會。于今始見，曠古希聞。〔臣某〕等幸列學官，叨趨輦路。有慚待問，空空然無地可逃；莫罄名言，蕩蕩乎惟天為大。涓埃何在，海嶽奚裨？伏願日就月將，冀聖學自今以始；河清海晏，祝
translation_en: …the Way. All enter the Great Learning: truly it is the gateway for worthy scholars. Joyful indeed is the Biyong, the place of moral teaching. Its walls rise several ren high, and its influence stirs the four quarters. For there must be those universally honored throughout the realm, yet Your Majesty, in your abundant virtue, has never deemed yourself a sage. The rites are enhanced by the offering of vegetables, your thoughts already communing silently with the First Teacher. Taking your place beneath the canopy in the lecture hall, you desire only to hear the Great Way. The Six Classics are all present, and the people gather round to behold you. Acting as their ruler and their teacher has now reached its fullest glory. How would we dare declare that you fall short of Yao or Shun? Though following established precedents, this is truly a splendid ceremony. In honoring your teachers and tutors with due ritual, your deeds surpass those of the Han emperor; in summoning eminent Confucian scholars in great numbers, your accomplishments exceed those of the Tang emperor. Majestically you reveal the direction of our Way; vigorously you magnify the spirit of this cultural tradition. Your beneficence extends equally to the Six Halls, which receive its moistening rain and dew; your radiance reaches all the officials, who rejoice in this fortunate meeting of wind and cloud. Only now have we witnessed such a thing, rarely heard of through all antiquity. [Your servant So-and-so] and the others are fortunate to rank among the education officials and privileged to approach the imperial carriage route. Ashamed to await your questions, we are empty of learning and have nowhere to hide; no words can exhaust our praise, for vast indeed is your greatness, matched only by Heaven. What can our tiny drops and specks of dust amount to? How can they add anything to the seas and mountains? We humbly wish that you advance daily and progress monthly, hoping that your sagely learning will take a new beginning from this day. With the Yellow River running clear and the seas tranquil, we pray…

title: 弘治二年廣東鄉試錄
text:
聖祖
純皇乎且自古帝王之一天下者非盛德無以
得民心非大功無以一海內堯舜禹湯文
武不容議矣漢唐宋能一天下者數君姑
未言也若夫四分五裂合而復分南國北
朝理而復亂紛紛擾擾又不必言矣然天
地不可以長夜日月不可以長晦是以掃
胡塵於六合開
帝業於萬年不能不有待於我
===
太祖高皇帝焉夫仁如帝堯學如孔子
聖祖之德至是無以加矣故千古之首稱必歸
之茅茨土階萬世之師法必歸之節用愛
人其仁如天至誠動物
聖祖之德與之為無間矣故諸將之諭惟安民
以仁之是言國珍之來必推誠相與而不
疑成湯代虐以寬其即討温台而戒湯和
以毋縱殺也文王為人君止於仁其即取
文石而折言者以為厲民也虜黑漢而遣
punctuated: 聖祖、純皇乎？且自古帝王之一天下者，非盛德無以得民心，非大功無以一海內。堯舜禹湯文武，不容議矣；漢唐宋能一天下者數君，姑未言也。若夫四分五裂，合而復分，南國北朝，理而復亂，紛紛擾擾，又不必言矣。然天地不可以長夜，日月不可以長晦。是以掃胡塵於六合，開帝業於萬年，不能不有待於我太祖高皇帝焉。夫仁如帝堯，學如孔子，聖祖之德至是無以加矣。故千古之首稱，必歸之茅茨土階；萬世之師法，必歸之節用愛人。其仁如天，至誠動物，聖祖之德與之為無間矣。故諸將之諭，惟安民以仁之是言；國珍之來，必推誠相與而不疑。成湯代虐以寬，其即討温台而戒湯和以毋縱殺也。文王為人君止於仁，其即取文石而折言者以為厲民也。虜黑漢而遣
translation_en:
…the Sacred Progenitor and Emperor Chun? Moreover, from antiquity, emperors and kings who unified All under Heaven could not win the people’s hearts without abundant virtue, nor unite all within the seas without great achievements. Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, King Wen, and King Wu are beyond dispute. Let us leave aside for now the few rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song who managed to unite All under Heaven. As for the fragmentation into rival states, reunification followed by renewed division, southern kingdoms and northern dynasties, order followed by renewed disorder—all that turmoil need not be discussed either. Yet Heaven and Earth could not remain in perpetual night, nor the sun and moon remain forever obscured. Thus, to sweep away the dust of foreign rule throughout the six directions and establish an imperial enterprise enduring for ten thousand years, the world inevitably had to await our Taizu, the Exalted Emperor.

Benevolent as Emperor Yao and learned as Confucius: the virtue of the Sacred Progenitor reached a height beyond which nothing could be added. Thus, the highest praise throughout the ages must go to thatched roofs and earthen steps; the model for ten thousand generations must be frugality in expenditure and love for the people. His benevolence was like Heaven, his utmost sincerity moved all beings: the Sacred Progenitor’s virtue was indistinguishable from theirs. Thus, his instructions to his generals spoke only of bringing peace to the people through benevolence; when Guozhen came to submit, he treated him with complete sincerity and without suspicion.
